definition_zh: 冒险事业；风险投资；动词：敢于去、冒险做；大胆提出
definition_en: a risky or daring enterprise, or to go somewhere or say something despite the danger
core_image: 一条小船离开熟悉的岸边，驶向看不清的雾里
scene: 天还没亮，几条渔船却已经解开缆绳驶向外海。Few boats ventured out in such heavy fog.
sceneCN: 这里 venture 是「冒险前往」（第 3 个义项：冒着风险去某处）；句意为浓雾之中很少有船敢出海。小船离岸驶入雾里，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险事业；风险投资；投机
动词：冒险前往；敢于做；大胆提出

collocations.zh: 冒昧地做某事；斗胆做某事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -some 构成，义为「好冒险的；敢于尝试的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「冒险者；合资经营参与者」
同源自拉丁语 advenire 的词，义为「冒险；奇遇」
与 adventure 同源，义为「爱冒险的」

senses.title: A daring enterprise
senses.titleCN: 冒险事业：有风险的事业
senses.definition: a new business activity or project that involves risk of loss
senses.definitionCN: 一项承担亏损风险的新生意或新项目
senses.example: Opening a shop in a quiet town was a bold venture.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷清的小镇开店是一次大胆的冒险事业。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come, and what is ventured is an outcome that has not yet come; you commit before you know it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，venture 的结果尚未到来；你在知道结果之前就已经下了注。

senses.title: Money put at risk
senses.titleCN: 风险投资：押上去的资本
senses.definition: money or capital invested in a risky project in the hope of large profit
senses.definitionCN: 投入有风险项目、期望高额回报的资金
senses.example: The firm put its first venture capital into a small software team.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司把第一笔风险投资投给了一个小型软件团队。
senses.why: The abstract enterprise becomes a sum of money: the risk is now measurable in cash.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的冒险事业化为具体的金额：风险此时可以用钱来衡量。

senses.title: To dare to go
senses.titleCN: 冒险前往：敢去某个地方
senses.definition: to go somewhere that may be dangerous or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 敢于前往可能危险或令人不快的地方
senses.example: No one ventured into the flooded tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人冒险进入那条被淹的隧道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the picture of leaving safe ground: the body moves first, the guarantee comes later or never.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了离开安全地面这一画面：身体先动，保障之后才来，也许永远不来。

senses.title: To dare to say
senses.definition: to say or suggest something that may be unwelcome or may be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 敢于说出可能不受欢迎或可能出错的话
senses.example: May I venture a different explanation?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以冒昧地提一个不同的解释吗？
senses.why: Speaking up is also a step into the open; the speaker risks being wrong in front of others.
senses.whyCN: 开口说话同样是走进开阔处；说话人要冒着在众人面前出错的风险。

senses.title: To try something new
senses.titleCN: 敢于尝试：试着做没做过的事
senses.definition: to attempt something new or difficult despite the chance of failure
senses.definitionCN: 尽管可能失败，仍尝试新事物或难做的事
senses.example: She ventured a smile at the stranger across the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝过道上那位陌生人试着笑了一下。
senses.why: The core image is small here but unchanged: a step taken without knowing how it will be received.
senses.whyCN: 这里的意象虽小却没有改变：在不知道会被如何接受的情况下迈出一步。

intro.en: Venture is a clipped form of adventure, which came from Latin through Old French; the family all turns on the verb 'to come'.
intro.cn: venture 是 adventure 的截短形式，后者经由古法语来自拉丁语；整个词族都围绕「来」这个动词。

items.en: The verb venire meant 'to come'; its future participle venturus described what is going to come.
items.cn: 动词 venire 意为「来」，其将来分词 venturus 指「将要到来的事」。

items.en: Medieval Latin adventura meant 'things about to happen', used for what fate would bring.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 adventura 意为「将要发生的事」，用来指命运会带来什么。

items.en: Old French aventure carried the sense of chance, hazard and a risky undertaking.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 带有「机遇、风险、冒险之举」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed aventure in the thirteenth century; the shorter venture split off as a separate word.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 aventure；较短的形式 venture 后来独立成一个词。

items.en: Commerce made venture a practical word: joint venture and venture capital name enterprises with money at risk.
items.cn: 商业让 venture 变成务实之词：joint venture 与 venture capital 都指押着钱的经营行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same 'come' family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns and verbs for risk-taking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「来」词根的一族词；近义组收表示冒险的名词与动词。

entries.definition: An exciting or dangerous experience; the longer form from which venture was cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险、奇遇」，是 venture 由之截短的较长形式。

entries.definition: Something that happens; literally that which comes out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件」，字面意思就是「出来的事」。

entries.definition: To stop something from coming about; pre- plus venire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻止」，由 pre- 加 venire「来」构成。

entries.definition: To devise something new; literally to come upon an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发明」，字面上是「碰上、遇见」一个想法。

entries.definition: The chance of loss itself; venture is the undertaking that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，指损失的可能性本身；venture 是承担风险的那件事。

entries.definition: To bet on an uncertain result; more openly about chance and money.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赌博、押注」，更直接地指机会与金钱。

entries.definition: A task or project one commits to, without the stress on danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承担的事业、任务」，不特别强调危险。

entries.definition: To be bold enough to do something frightening; the nerve rather than the project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「敢于」，强调胆量而非事业本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb venire and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 venire，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: venture is adventure without the ad: the same risky trip, said shorter.
normal.cn: venture 就是去掉 ad 的 adventure：同一趟冒险，说得更短。

normal.en: Joint venture is a business born of two partners, both risking money.
normal.cn: joint venture 是两家合作生出的生意，双方都押了钱。

normal.en: Venture capital names money that dares to fund an unproven idea.
normal.cn: venture capital 指敢去资助尚未验证的想法的钱。

normal.en: To venture out is to leave the house when the weather warns against it.
normal.cn: venture out 就是在天气示警时仍走出家门。

normal.en: Nothing ventured, nothing gained: no risk taken means no gain made.
normal.cn: 不入虎穴焉得虎子：不承担风险就得不到收获。

abstract.en: See the word as a boat leaving the harbour: the shore is the known, the fog is the coming, and the boat moves before it can see.
abstract.cn: 把这个词想成一条离港的小船：岸是已知，雾是将要到来的事，而船在看清之前就已经出发。

abstract.en: Everything in the word happens before the result arrives: venture is always on the side of the untested.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的事都发生在结果到来之前：venture 永远站在未经检验的一边。

abstract.en: The same move can be a business, a journey or a sentence; all three are steps into the open.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作可以是一桩生意、一段路程或一句话；三者都是走进开阔处的一步。

examples.en: They launched a small venture selling solar lamps to remote villages.
examples.cn: 他们创办了一家小型企业，向偏远村庄销售太阳能灯。

examples.en: Nobody ventured outside until the storm had passed.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过去之前，没有人敢出门。

examples.en: The two firms formed a joint venture to build the bridge.
examples.cn: 这两家公司组建合资企业来修建这座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万一扯」——船万一被扯离岸边，就只能往前闯：冒险

root: 为 adventure 的截短形式，源自拉丁语 venire「来」的将来分词 venturus「将要来临的」，经中世纪拉丁语 adventura 与古法语 aventure 进入英语；同族词有 event、prevent、invent。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of venture run from the abstract enterprise to the capital behind it, then to the small daily daring of going, saying and trying.
sensesIntro.cn: venture 的五个义项从抽象的冒险事业出发，到其背后的资本，再到出门、开口、试探这些日常里的小胆量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat leaves the shore and steers into fog before it can see the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条船离开岸边，在看清对岸之前就驶进雾里。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the risky project and the capital that funds it.
branches.cn: 资本线：冒险的项目以及资助它的资金。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the feet move into a place that may harm them.
branches.cn: 身体线：双脚走进可能有害的地方。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the mouth risks a remark that may be wrong.
branches.cn: 声音线：嘴巴冒着出错的风险说出看法。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: the smallest step, a smile offered to a stranger.
branches.cn: 姿态线：最小的一步，比如向陌生人递出的微笑。

branches.en: CONTRAST: adventure is the same word with more colour, venture the cooler business face.
branches.cn: 对照线：adventure 更带色彩，venture 则是更冷静的商业面孔。

intro.en: Venture inherits a Latin verb stem plus English endings; its parts are transparent once the family is known.
intro.cn: venture 继承了拉丁语动词词干并接英语词尾；认识这个词族之后，各部分都很清楚。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is verifiable: venire, to come, with its participle venturus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：venire「来」及其分词 venturus。

items.example: It carries the core of the word.
It turns the verb stem into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成名词。

definition_zh: 口头的；言语的；与词语有关的；逐字的；动词的
definition_en: relating to words, especially words that are spoken rather than written
core_image: 一串声音从嘴里出来，在空中排成可数的词，再落进对方的耳朵
scene: 面试结束前，主考官提醒候选人把口头承诺写成邮件，他说：Please put your verbal promise in writing.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「口头说出的、以说话方式作出的」（第 1 个义项：以口头表达而非书面写下）；句意为主考官请候选人把口头承诺落实为书面文字。

pos.zh: 口头的；言语的；词语的；逐字的；动词的
动词性词语（如动名词、动词性名词）

derivatives.zh: 口头地；用言语地
用言语表达；使成词语
言语化；用词语表达的过程
言辞表达；拘泥字面的说法
擅长言辞的人；拘泥字面者

senses.title: Spoken rather than written
senses.titleCN: 口头说出的，而非写下的
senses.definition: expressed in speech rather than in writing
senses.definitionCN: 以口头说出而不是以书面形式表达的
senses.example: She gave a verbal warning instead of a written one.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了口头警告，而没有发出书面警告。
senses.why: The root means 'word', and when a word is contrasted with a written document, the channel that remains is the voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根意为「词」；当它与书面文件相对时，剩下的渠道就是说话的声音。

senses.title: Relating to words or language
senses.definition: concerned with words and with the ability to use them
senses.definitionCN: 与词语以及运用词语的能力有关的
senses.example: Verbal ability predicts later reading success.
senses.exampleCN: 言语能力可以预测日后的阅读表现。
senses.why: The adjective was formed from the Latin noun for 'word', so its broadest job is simply to label anything that has to do with words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由表示「词」的拉丁名词构成，因此最宽的用法就是给一切与词语有关的事物贴标签。

senses.title: Word-for-word and literal
senses.definition: following the exact words of an original rather than its overall meaning
senses.definitionCN: 照着原文的每一个词，而不是照着整体意思
senses.example: A verbal translation often misses the tone of the original.
senses.exampleCN: 逐字翻译常常丢掉原文的语气。
senses.why: If each word is handled separately, the translation becomes a row of separate words rather than one living sentence.
senses.whyCN: 若把每个词单独处理，译文就成了一排孤立的词，而不是一句活的话。

senses.title: Relating to a verb in grammar
senses.definition: relating to a verb or to a form built from a verb
senses.definitionCN: 与动词有关，或与由动词构成的形式有关
senses.example: The verbal ending changes with tense and person.
senses.exampleCN: 动词词尾随时态与人称变化。
senses.why: Latin used the same noun for 'word' and for 'verb', because the verb is the word that carries the action of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用同一个名词既指「词」也指「动词」，因为动词是承载句子动作的那个词。

senses.title: Using too many words
senses.definition: using more words than are needed to make a point
senses.definitionCN: 表达一个意思时用了超出需要的词
senses.example: His verbal style buried the main point under qualifications.
senses.exampleCN: 他冗长的说话方式把重点埋在一堆限定语下面。
senses.why: A person who piles up words is still working with words, but the abundance itself becomes the noticeable quality.
senses.whyCN: 堆词的人仍然在处理词语，只是词语的数量本身成了最显眼的特点。

senses.title: Words without matching action
senses.titleCN: 只有言辞而没有行动的
senses.definition: expressed in words but not supported by real action
senses.definitionCN: 只用言辞表达，却没有实际行动支撑
senses.example: The agreement was merely verbal and was never carried out.
senses.exampleCN: 那项约定只是口头上的，从未落实。
senses.why: When words are set against deeds, calling something verbal is a way of saying that only the talking half exists.
senses.whyCN: 当词语与行动相对时，说某事只是口头上的，就等于说只有说话那一半存在。

senses.title: Oral in a legal sense
senses.titleCN: 法律意义上的口头形式
senses.definition: made by speech rather than set down in a written instrument
senses.definitionCN: 以说话方式作出，而不是写在正式文书里
senses.example: A verbal contract can still bind the parties in some cases.
senses.exampleCN: 在某些情形下，口头合同仍能约束双方。
senses.why: Law separates a spoken declaration from a signed paper, and the word marks the side that leaves no written record.
senses.whyCN: 法律把口头声明与签字文件分开，这个词标记的正是没有留下书面记录的那一边。

senses.title: Carried by words, not by gestures
senses.titleCN: 以词语而非手势传递的
senses.definition: communicated through words rather than through bodily signals
senses.definitionCN: 通过词语而不是通过身体信号传递的
senses.example: The verbal message was clear, but the gestures softened it.
senses.exampleCN: 言语信息很清楚，但手势让它变得柔和。
senses.why: Communication research splits a message into the word channel and the body channel, and this sense names the word channel.
senses.whyCN: 交流研究把一次信息分成词语渠道与身体渠道，这个义项命名的正是词语渠道。

intro.en: Verbal comes through Middle French from Late Latin verbalis 'of words', built on Latin verbum 'word'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: verbal 经中古法语来自晚期拉丁语 verbalis「词的」，由拉丁语 verbum「词」加形容词后缀构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Verbum meant 'word' and was also the grammar term for 'verb'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link often suggested to an Indo-European root for speaking is a reconstruction, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: verbum 意为「词」，在语法中也指「动词」。其更深来源未得到证明；常有人把它系于某个表示「说话」的印欧词根，那只是重构形式，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The adjective verbalis 'relating to words' was formed from verbum and passed into learned usage.
items.cn: 形容词 verbalis「与词有关的」由 verbum 构成，并进入学术用语。

items.en: Middle French verbal carried the adjective into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the broad sense 'of words'.
items.cn: 中古法语 verbal 在十四世纪末把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于「与词有关的」这一宽泛意义。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word was regularly opposed to written, naming what is said aloud instead of what is set down on paper.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已常与「书面的」相对，指口头说出而非写在纸上的内容。

items.en: The grammatical sense 'of a verb' appears in the seventeenth century, and the noun for a verb-derived form developed later.
items.cn: 「与动词有关的」这一语法义在十七世纪出现，指动词性形式的名词义随后发展出来。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of the spoken sense is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of verbum remains unsettled, so any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：口头义的确切首见年代没有定论，verbum 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to verbal but follow different roots or different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近、但词根或前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built on the same Latin word for 'word', but it means in exactly the same words, word for word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁语表示「词」的词，但意思是「逐字地、一字不差地」。

entries.definition: From a Latin adjective meaning 'full of words'; it describes speech or writing that uses far too many words.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「充满词」的拉丁形容词，形容说话或写作用了过多词语。

entries.definition: It looks like a relative of the word root, but it comes from a Latin word for a home-born slave, later 'native'; it names the everyday language of a place.
entries.definitionCN: 外形像同族词，其实来自拉丁语指「家中出生的奴仆」、后转指「本地的」一词；它指一个地方日常使用的语言。

entries.definition: It descends from the same word stock through French and means an excess of words, often empty or official wording.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语同出这一词群，意思是词语过量，常指空洞或官样文字。

entries.definition: The standard adjective for what is spoken rather than written; it comes from a different Latin root meaning 'mouth'.
entries.definitionCN: 指口头而非书面的标准形容词；它来自另一个意为「嘴」的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: The ordinary English participle for language produced by voice; it is plainer than verbal and lacks the grammatical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指用嗓音说出的语言的普通英语分词，比 verbal 朴素，也没有那些语法义。

entries.definition: Relating to language as a system; verbal can focus narrowly on individual words.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为系统的语言有关；verbal 可以只聚焦于一个个词。

entries.definition: A plain adjective for writing or speech that uses too many words, close to the fifth sense of verbal.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话或写作词句过多的朴素形容词，接近 verbal 的第 5 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real contrasts and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的对比与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'word', so verbal is the adjective for anything word-shaped.
normal.cn: 词根意为「词」，因此这个词就是给一切「词形状」的事物作形容词。

normal.en: The same root yields the adverb meaning word for word and the adjective meaning full of words.
normal.cn: 同一词根还构成表示「逐字地」的副词与表示「满口是词」的形容词。

normal.en: Contrast pair: a verbal promise is spoken, while a written promise is on paper.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：口头的承诺用嘴说，书面的承诺落在纸上。

normal.en: Grammar note: a verbal noun is a noun built from a verb, such as a gerund.
normal.cn: 语法提示：动词性名词是由动词构成的名词，如动名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spoken sense: verbal agreement, verbal abuse, verbal skills.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「口头」义：口头协议、言语辱骂、语言能力。

abstract.en: Picture words as small stones a speaker hands over one by one.
abstract.cn: 把词语想成说话人一颗颗递过去的小石子。

abstract.en: Picture a signed page and a spoken sentence placed on two sides of a scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签好的纸和一句说出的话被放在天平两端。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence made only of separate bricks, with no mortar between them.

sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个起点出发，即「词」这个单位，然后按渠道分叉：口说、书写、语法、逐字、冗长、无行动支撑、法律形式与身体信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken word leaving the mouth as a small, countable object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个说出的词像可数的小物件一样离开嘴巴。

branches.en: SPOKEN CHANNEL: both the everyday warning and the legal declaration exist only in voice.
branches.cn: 口头渠道：日常警告与法律声明都只存在于声音里。

branches.en: WORD CARRIER: words themselves carry the message, whether against gestures or as a general ability.
branches.cn: 词语载体：无论与手势相对，还是作为一般能力，承载信息的都是词语本身。

branches.en: ONE WORD AT A TIME: literal translation treats each word as a separate unit.
branches.cn: 逐词处理：逐字翻译把每个词当作独立单位。

branches.en: VERB AND VERBOSITY: the same root names the action word and the habit of piling words up.
branches.cn: 动词与冗词：同一词根既命名动作词，也命名堆词的毛病。

branches.en: WORD WITHOUT DEED: the promise exists in speech but never becomes an act.
branches.cn: 有言无行：承诺只存在于言语中，从未变成行动。

intro.en: Verbal is built from a Latin root and a Latin adjectival suffix, and the same pieces recur across a small but active word family.
intro.cn: verbal 由一个拉丁词根与一个拉丁形容词后缀构成，同样的部件反复出现在一个小而活跃的词族里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbum 'word' supplies verbal, verbatim, verbose, proverb and verb; the suffix -alis marks the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「词」的词根衍生出表示「言语的」「逐字的」「啰嗦的」「谚语」「动词」的一组词；形容词后缀标记关系。

definition_zh: 裁决；评断；结论；（陪审团或验尸官的）裁定
definition_en: the formal decision of a jury or an official inquiry, or any opinion reached after weighing the evidence
core_image: 十二个人从一间小屋里走出来，领头的人把一张折好的纸条递到书记员手里
scene: 十二个人在小屋里商议了四个小时，领头的人把写有结论的纸条交给书记员。The foreman handed the verdict to the clerk after four hours of deliberation.
sceneCN: 这里 verdict 指「陪审团经商议后作出的正式结论」（第 1 个义项：陪审团裁决）；句意为商议四小时后，领头的人把裁决结果交给书记员。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、陪审席、书记员的登记册、法庭围栏。

senses.title: A jury's decision
senses.definition: the formal finding of a jury on whether the accused is guilty or not guilty
senses.definitionCN: 陪审团就被指控者有罪与否作出的正式结论
senses.example: The foreman handed the verdict to the clerk after four hours of deliberation.
senses.exampleCN: 商议四小时后，领头的人把裁决结果交给书记员。
senses.why: Verdict is vere 'truly' plus dictum 'saying': the word originally meant a true statement, and the jury's function is to say what it holds to be true about the facts.
senses.whyCN: verdict 是 vere「真实地」加 dictum「陈述」：这个词原意是一句真话，而陪审团的职能正是说出它对事实所认定的真相。

senses.title: A finding of an inquiry
senses.titleCN: 调查或验尸得出的结论
senses.definition: the conclusion recorded by an official inquiry, such as a coroner's finding on a death
senses.definitionCN: 官方调查所记录的结论，如验尸官对死因的认定
senses.example: The coroner returned a verdict of accidental death.
senses.exampleCN: 验尸官作出意外死亡的裁定。
senses.why: An inquiry speaks in the same voice as a jury: it states what it finds to be true, so the noun serves both without strain.
senses.whyCN: 调查与陪审团以同一种口吻发言：它陈述自己认定的事实，因此这个名词无需费力就能适用于两者。

senses.title: A considered opinion
senses.definition: any judgement reached after weighing evidence, even where no court is involved
senses.definitionCN: 经权衡证据后作出判断，即使不涉及法院
senses.example: Our verdict, after three months of testing, is that the material is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 经过三个月测试，我们的结论是这种材料可靠。
senses.why: Once a verdict is simply a true saying, it can be pronounced by anyone who has done the weighing, not only by twelve sworn citizens.
senses.whyCN: 既然裁决不过是一句真实的话，任何做过权衡的人都可以作出，而不必是十二名宣誓的公民。

senses.title: The public's judgement
senses.titleCN: 公众或媒体对人的评价
senses.definition: the opinion formed about a person, product or event by the public at large
senses.definitionCN: 公众对某人、某产品或某事件形成的看法
senses.example: The verdict on the new bridge was favourable long before it opened.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新桥远在通车之前就已获得好评。
senses.why: The metaphor puts the public in the jury box: collective opinion borrows the finality of a court's word.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把公众放进陪审席：集体意见借用了法庭话语的终局性。

senses.title: An official review decision in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育复核后的官方判定
senses.definition: a final decision by a reviewing official or video panel on what happened in play
senses.definitionCN: 复核官员或视频裁判组对场上事实作出的最终判定
senses.example: The video panel's verdict overturned the goal within thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 视频裁判组在三十秒内推翻了进球判定。
senses.why: Sport has added review panels that pronounce on facts, and they borrow the word because their finding must end the argument.
senses.whyCN: 体育增设了对事实作出宣告的复核小组，它们借用了这个词，因为其结论必须终结争论。

senses.title: A decision on a submitted work
senses.titleCN: 对提交作品的最终评定
senses.definition: the final decision of a panel on an entry or application
senses.definitionCN: 评审团对参赛作品或申请作出的最终决定
senses.example: The jury's verdict placed the design second in its category.
senses.exampleCN: 评审团的评定把该设计排在其类别第二。
senses.why: A competition needs a pronouncement that ends the comparison, and the courtroom noun supplies the finality.
senses.whyCN: 比赛需要一个终结比较的宣告，而法庭名词正好提供这种终局性。

senses.title: The outcome of a test or comparison
senses.titleCN: 测试或比较得出的结局性结论
senses.definition: the conclusion produced by a test, comparison or long observation
senses.definitionCN: 测试、比较或长期观察所得出的结论
senses.example: Field trials gave a clear verdict: the treated plots held water longer.
senses.exampleCN: 田间试验给出明确结论：处理过的地块保水更久。
senses.why: The noun is used for anything that finally settles a question, because settling is what the original word meant.
senses.whyCN: 凡能最终了结一个问题的事物都用这个名词，因为「了结」正是原词之义。

senses.title: A verdict read as a sentence
senses.titleCN: 裁决作为判词/量刑依据
senses.definition: the formal answer of guilty or not guilty, on which sentence then follows
senses.definitionCN: 有罪或无罪的形式回答，随后据以量刑
senses.example: The verdict was not guilty, and the court had nothing left to impose.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决为无罪，法院也就无从量刑。
senses.why: English keeps verdict for the answer and sentence for the consequence, a division that legal usage has held for centuries.
senses.whyCN: 英语用 verdict 指回答，用 sentence 指后果，这一区分法律用法已维持数百年。

intro.en: Verdict comes through Anglo-French verdit from Latin veredictum, built on vere 'truly' plus dictum 'saying'. The word meant a true statement before it meant a jury's answer.
intro.cn: verdict 经英属法语 verdit 来自拉丁 veredictum，由 vere「真实地」加 dictum「陈述」构成。这个词先指真实的陈述，后指陪审团的回答。

items.en: Verus meant true, and its adverb vere meant truly; the same root gives veritas and the English verity.
items.cn: verus 意为真的，其副词 vere 意为真实地；同一词根还给 veritas 与英语 verity。

items.en: Dictum was a thing said, from dicere 'to say'; in legal Latin it named a formal statement rather than casual speech.
items.cn: dictum 是所说的话，出自 dicere「说」；在法律拉丁中它指正式陈述，而非随意言谈。

items.en: Veredictum meant a true declaration; the compound is usually read as 'truly said', though the exact force of the first element is a matter of interpretation.
items.cn: veredictum 意为真实的宣告；这个复合词通常被理解为「真实地说出」，不过第一个成分的确切作用属解释问题。

items.en: Anglo-French verdit narrowed the word to the answer a jury gives, which is how English received it in the medieval period.
items.cn: 英属法语 verdit 把这个词收窄为陪审团给出的回答，英语在中世纪正是这样接收它的。

items.en: By the early modern period verdict was fixed to the jury's finding, with ruling and judgment covering the court's own decisions.
items.cn: 到近代早期，verdict 已固定为陪审团的认定，而法院自己的决定由 ruling 与 judgment 承担。

items.en: The first English date is approximate: medieval use is recorded, but the earliest citation in English texts is not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 英语首见年代为约数：中世纪用例已有记录，但英语文本中的最早书证没有精确年代。

note.en: The first group shares the 'saying' stem or looks close to it; the second group names decisions that are often mistaken for a verdict.
note.cn: 第一组共享「说」这一词干或形近；第二组是常被误当作裁决的其他决定。

entries.definition: A formal saying or pronouncement, from the same dictum; it carries no decision and binds nobody.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的说法或宣告，同出 dictum；它不含决定，也不约束任何人。

entries.definition: To say beforehand, from dicere; it is about the future and needs no evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 预先说出，出自 dicere；它关于未来，不需要证据。

entries.definition: To check that something is true, from verus; it tests a claim rather than settling it.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实，出自 verus；它检验说法，而非了结它。

entries.definition: Truth or a true statement, from verus; an abstract noun with no courtroom role.
entries.definitionCN: 真理或真实的陈述，出自 verus；抽象名词，无法庭职能。

entries.definition: From ius 'right', not verus; it names fairness, not a finding.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 ius「权利」而非 verus；命名公平，而非认定。

entries.definition: The court's decision on law or procedure; it answers the judge's question, while verdict answers the jury's.
entries.definitionCN: 法院就法律或程序作出的决定；它回答法官的问题，而 verdict 回答陪审团的问题。

entries.definition: The full decision including reasons and order; verdict is only the answer to the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 包含理由与命令的完整决定；verdict 只是对被控罪名的回答。

entries.definition: The penalty imposed after a verdict; it is the consequence, never the finding.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决之后所施加的处罚；它是后果，绝不是认定。

entries.definition: The conclusion of an investigation or tribunal, which may or may not be phrased as a verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 调查或裁判所的结论，可能以裁决的措辞表达，也可能不。

entries.definition: Any settled choice, from a court or from a committee; it lacks the jury flavour of verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 任何已定的选择，可出自法院或委员会；它不带陪审团色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin true and saying, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「真」与「陈述」、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Vere is 'truly' and dictum is 'saying', so a verdict is a true saying, the sentence that settles what the facts are.
normal.cn: vere 是「真实地」，dictum 是「陈述」，所以裁决就是一句真话，一句了结事实的话。

normal.en: The family runs verdict, dictum, predict, verify, verity and veracious.
normal.cn: 同族词有 verdict、dictum、predict、verify、verity 与 veracious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the courtroom sense: reach a verdict, a guilty verdict, return a verdict.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法庭义：作出裁决、有罪裁决、宣布裁决。

normal.en: A verdict is the answer, a sentence is the consequence; English has kept them apart for centuries.
normal.cn: 裁决是回答，量刑是后果；英语数百年来把两者分开。

normal.en: Anyone who has weighed the evidence can issue a verdict, which is why the word escaped the courtroom.
normal.cn: 任何权衡过证据的人都能作出裁决，这个词正是因此走出了法庭。

abstract.en: Picture a folded slip of paper passed through a hatch before anyone speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折好的纸条在所有人开口之前从窗口递出。

abstract.en: Picture twelve chairs pushed back at once, and the corridor filling with waiting people.
abstract.cn: 想象十二把椅子同时被推开，走廊里立刻挤满等候的人。

abstract.en: Picture a set of scales coming to rest, and the room deciding to believe the pointer.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平静止下来，屋子里的人都决定相信那根指针。

examples.en: The jury reached its verdict after two days.
examples.cn: 陪审团在两天后作出了裁决。

examples.en: Historians have not yet delivered a verdict on that treaty.
examples.cn: 历史学者尚未对那项条约给出定论。

examples.en: The inquest recorded an open verdict because the cause was unclear.
examples.cn: 因死因不明，验尸庭记录了存疑裁决。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ver（真）+ dict（说）」——一句被认定为真的话 → 裁决

root: 拉丁 verus「真」的副词 vere「真实地」+ dictum「陈述」（出自 dicere「说」）→ veredictum「真实宣告」→ 英属法语 verdit → 英语 verdict。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one slip of paper: a jury writes it, an inquiry copies it, anyone who has weighed evidence can pronounce it, the public adopts it, a video panel borrows it, a competition uses it, a field trial produces it, and a court then decides what follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一张纸条：陪审团写下它，调查照抄它，任何权衡过证据的人都能说出它，公众采纳它，视频裁判组借用它，比赛使用它，田间试验产出它，最后由法院决定接下来怎么办。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded slip handed through a hatch before anyone in the room speaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折好的纸条在屋里所有人开口之前从窗口递出。

branches.en: TWO OFFICIAL VOICES: a jury and an inquiry both state what they find to be true.
branches.cn: 两种官方声音：陪审团与调查都在陈述它们认定的真相。

branches.en: FROM COURT TO PUBLIC: once it is simply a true saying, the public can speak it too.
branches.cn: 从法庭到公众：既然它只是一句真话，公众也能说。

branches.en: PANELS OF TWO KINDS: sport and competitions borrow the word because their finding must end the argument.
branches.cn: 两种评审团：体育与比赛借用这个词，因为其结论必须终结争论。

branches.en: THE TEST SPEAKS: a field trial can deliver a verdict, since settling a question is the original sense.
branches.cn: 试验发言：田间试验也能给出裁决，因为「了结问题」正是原义。

branches.en: THE ANSWER AND THE PRICE: the verdict answers the charge, and sentence pays for it.
branches.cn: 回答与代价：裁决回答指控，量刑为其付出代价。

intro.en: Verdict is two Latin words fused: an adverb of truth and a noun of saying. Both halves are productive elsewhere in English.
intro.cn: verdict 是两个拉丁词融合而成：一个表真的副词与一个表陈述的名词，两半在英语别处都有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus gives verify, verity and veracious; dicere gives dictum, predict and contradict; the fusion gives verdict alone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 verus 给出 verify、verity 与 veracious；dicere 给出 dictum、predict 与 contradict；融合形式只给出 verdict。

definition_zh: 核实；验证；查证；确认；证明为真；身份核验；合规审查；（哲学）证实原则
definition_en: the act of checking or proving that something is true, accurate, or genuine
core_image: 一枚印章落在核对过的文件末尾，旁边是逐条打勾的清单
scene: 审核员把每一张发票与合同逐条对照，确认金额和日期都能对上，才在末页盖章。Before payment, the clerk carried out a careful verification of every invoice against the contract.
sceneCN: 这里指逐条核对材料是否真实、准确（第 1 个义项：核实、查证）；句意为付款前职员把每张发票与合同仔细核对了一遍。场景图取象：核对完的文件末尾落下一枚印章。

证明为真的证据或确认结论

derivatives.zh: 核实；证实（由「真」与「做」两个拉丁词根合成，字面即「使之成真」）
可核实的（加表示「能够被……」的形容词后缀，指可以被查证）
可核实性（在形容词后加表示「性质」的名词后缀）

senses.title: The act of checking
senses.definition: the act of checking whether a statement, figure or account is true and accurate
senses.definitionCN: 检查某一说法、数字或账目是否真实准确的行为
senses.example: Verification of the figures took three days.
senses.exampleCN: 核对这些数字花了三天。
senses.why: The word joins 'true' and 'make', so the act is making sure a claim really is true.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「真」与「做」合在一起，动作就是确保某个说法确实为真。

senses.title: Formal confirmation
senses.definition: official confirmation that a document, claim or record meets a required standard
senses.definitionCN: 官方确认某份文件、声明或记录达到了规定标准
senses.example: The certificate requires verification by a public notary.
senses.exampleCN: 这份证书需要由公证人正式确认。
senses.why: Institutions need a stamp as well as a check, and the word covers both the check and the resulting confirmation.
senses.whyCN: 机构既要查也要盖章，这个词同时涵盖查验与由此得到的确认。

senses.title: Evidence that proves
senses.definition: a piece of evidence or a statement that establishes something as true
senses.definitionCN: 能证明某事为真的证据或说法
senses.example: His notes served as verification of the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笔记成了这一说法的凭据。
senses.why: The noun can name the proof itself, not only the act of producing it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指证据本身，而不只是取得证据的动作。

senses.title: Checking who you are
senses.definition: the process of confirming a person's identity, account or credentials before granting access
senses.definitionCN: 在给予权限之前确认某人身份、账户或凭证的程序
senses.example: Two-step verification blocked the stolen password.
senses.exampleCN: 两步核验挡住了被盗的密码。
senses.why: Digital accounts made this the everyday sense: a second check that the person is who the password says.
senses.whyCN: 数字账户使这一义项成为日常用法：再查一次，看人是否真如密码所称。

senses.title: Test against reality
senses.definition: confirmation of a scientific claim by independent observation, measurement or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过独立观察、测量或实验来确认某一科学主张
senses.example: Independent verification is the price of a published result.
senses.exampleCN: 独立验证是一项结果得以发表的代价。
senses.why: Science separates the claim from the claimant by asking another laboratory to check it.
senses.whyCN: 科学把主张与主张者分开，办法是让另一个实验室去查。

senses.title: Proof that software obeys its spec
senses.definition: the process of showing that a program or system has been built according to its stated requirements
senses.definitionCN: 证明某个程序或系统是按其声明的需求建成的过程
senses.example: Verification caught the error before the release.
senses.exampleCN: 验证在发布前抓住了这个错误。
senses.why: Engineering distinguishes building the thing right from building the right thing, and calls the first verification.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把「把东西做对」与「做对的东西」分开，前者称为验证。

senses.title: Audit of accounts
senses.definition: a formal audit of records, accounts or compliance with rules
senses.definitionCN: 对记录、账目或规则遵守情况的正式审查
senses.example: The agency ordered verification of the charity's spending.
senses.exampleCN: 主管机构下令核查该慈善机构的开支。
senses.why: Public money brings a legal duty to check, and the word acquired an administrative weight.
senses.whyCN: 公共资金带来核对的法定义务，这个词因此带上行政分量。

senses.title: Fact-checking before print
senses.definition: the editorial process of checking names, dates and quotations before publication
senses.definitionCN: 发表前核对人名、日期与引文的编辑程序
senses.example: The magazine's verification desk flagged two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志的核实台标出了两个日期问题。
senses.why: Publishing houses built a desk for this work, and the word named both the desk and its task.
senses.whyCN: 出版社为此设了专岗，这个词既指这个岗位，也指它的工作。

senses.title: The verification principle
senses.definition: the philosophical rule that a statement is meaningful only if it can be checked by experience
senses.definitionCN: 一种哲学主张：一个陈述只有能被经验检验才有意义
senses.example: The verification principle turned out to be too strict for its own rule.
senses.exampleCN: 证实原则对自己那条规则来说过于严格。
senses.why: Early twentieth-century philosophy tried to make meaning a testable property, and gave the word this narrow sense.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪初的哲学想把意义变成可检验的属性，于是给了这个词一个狭窄的义项。

intro.en: Verification is built from the Latin verus 'true' and facere 'to make', through Medieval Latin verificare. The chain is well documented and the only uncertain point is the exact date of its English entry.
intro.cn: verification 由拉丁语 verus「真」与 facere「做」构成，经由中世纪拉丁语 verificare 而来。词源链记录充分，唯一不确定的是它进入英语的确切年代。

items.en: Verus meant true or genuine, and it stands behind verity, veracity and the English word very.
items.cn: verus 意为真实的、真正的，还构成 verity、veracity 以及英语的 very。

items.en: The verb facere, to make or do, supplies the second half of the compound and the -fication ending.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为做、造，提供复合词的后半与 -fication 这一词尾。

items.en: Verificare meant to make true or to prove true, a word of the schools rather than of everyday speech.
items.cn: verificare 意为使之成真或证明为真，是学院用语而非日常口语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the late Middle Ages, first in learned and legal writing; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在中世纪晚期进入英语，最早见于学术与法律文本；确切年代不确定。

items.en: From the seventeenth century it spread into experiment and jurisprudence, where a claim must be checked by evidence.
items.cn: 十七世纪以后，它扩展到实验与法学领域，那里主张必须靠证据核查。

items.en: In the last decades it became a household word through codes, passwords and two-step checks.
items.cn: 近几十年，它靠验证码、密码与两步核验成了家常词汇。

note.en: The first group shares the true-making root or merely looks close; the second group contains the neighbouring checks that are often confused with verification.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「使真」词根，或只是字形相近；第二组是常与「验证」混淆的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to check or prove that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：核查或证明某事为真。

entries.definition: Truthfulness, especially of a person or account; it shares verus but not facere.
entries.definitionCN: 真实性、诚实，尤指人或陈述；共享「真」词根，不含「做」。

entries.definition: An old word for truth itself, built on the same Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指真理本身的古词，由同一个拉丁形容词构成。

entries.definition: The art of turning prose into verse; it looks close but comes from versus, a turning of the plough.
entries.definitionCN: 把散文写成诗句的技艺；字形相近，却来自「犁沟转向」之意的 versus。

entries.definition: Abusive speech that lowers someone's name; its first element means cheap or base.
entries.definitionCN: 贬损他人名誉的辱骂；其前一部分意为低贱。

entries.definition: Checking that a system meets the user's real need, as opposed to its written specification.
entries.definitionCN: 检查系统是否满足使用者的真实需要，与书面规格相对。

entries.definition: A statement or act that makes something formally certain.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事在形式上确定的说法或举动。

entries.definition: Proving that a person or object is genuine, especially in computing.
entries.definitionCN: 证明人或物为真品，尤用于计算机领域。

entries.definition: Formal granting of a certificate after an authority has checked a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 主管机构查过标准后正式发给证书。

entries.definition: The journalistic routine of confirming details before publication.
entries.definitionCN: 发表前核对细节的新闻例行工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real true-making root, the real derivative family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「使真」词根、真实派生词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Verus is true and facere is make, so verification is literally the making true of a claim.
normal.cn: 前者为真，后者为做，合起来字面就是使一个说法成真。

normal.en: The same true root gives verity and veracity, while the make root gives -fication in dozens of words.
normal.cn: 同一个「真」词根给出 verity 与 veracity，「做」词根则在许多词里留下 -fication 词尾。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: identity verification, independent verification, verification code.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：身份核验、独立核实、验证码。

normal.en: The verb is verify, the adjective verifiable, the person verifier.
normal.cn: 动词是 verify，形容词是可核实的，执行者是核验者。

normal.en: A verified document carries a stamp; a verification is the check that earns the stamp.
normal.cn: 已核实的文件带着印章，核验就是挣来这枚印章的检查。

abstract.en: Verification is distrust put to work in an orderly way.
abstract.cn: 核验是把不信任按规矩使出来。

abstract.en: It does not create truth; it only refuses to accept a claim until the claim can be checked.
abstract.cn: 它并不制造真理，只是在说法可被核对之前拒绝接受它。

abstract.en: A society that stops verifying slowly loses the difference between a claim and a fact.
abstract.cn: 一个不再核验的社会，会慢慢失去主张与事实之间的区别。

examples.en: Verification of the sample took longer than the test itself.
examples.cn: 样本核验比测试本身花的时间还长。

examples.en: The bank asks for a second verification before large transfers.
examples.cn: 大额转账前银行要求再做一次核验。

examples.en: Independent verification is what turns an announcement into a result.
examples.cn: 独立验证才能把一则宣告变成一个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「维瑞菲克申」——把「真」做出来，逐条打勾盖章：核实、验证

root: 中世纪拉丁语 verificare「使之成真、证明为真」← 拉丁语 verus「真」＋ facere「做、造」；verus 另构成 verity、veracity 与 very，facere 构成 -fication 系列。进入英语的确切年代不确定，义项扩展至科学、法律与数字身份。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the same act: a check, a formal confirmation, the proof itself, an identity check, a test against reality, proof of a specification, an audit, editorial fact-checking, and a philosophical principle.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个动作：核对、正式确认、凭据本身、身份核验、用事实检验、对规格的证明、账目审查、刊前核实，以及一条哲学原则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a checked list with ticks beside every line, and a stamp waiting at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：每行都打了勾的清单，末尾等着落下一枚印章。

branches.en: THE CHECK AND ITS PROOF: the act of testing a claim, and the evidence that the test produced.
branches.cn: 检查及其凭据：检验主张的动作，以及检验得出的证据。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL SEAL: confirmation by an authority, and the audit that must come before it.
branches.cn: 官方印章：主管者的确认，以及确认之前必须做的审查。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY CHECK: the second step that proves a person is who the account says.
branches.cn: 身份核验：证明人如其账户所称的第二步。

branches.en: THE TEST OF A CLAIM: independent experiment, a program checked against its specification, and a page checked before print.
branches.cn: 对主张的检验：独立实验、按规格检查的程序，以及付印前核对过的稿件。

branches.en: THE PRINCIPLE: meaning itself is said to require a possible check.
branches.cn: 那条原则：意义本身被要求可以被检验。

intro.en: Verification is a compound of two productive Latin pieces, and its endings still build abstract nouns in English.
intro.cn: verification 由两个能产的拉丁构件合成，其词尾在英语中仍能造抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus and facere are the two sources; the noun ending came through Medieval Latin -ficatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verus 与 facere 是两个来源，名词词尾经由中世纪拉丁语的 -ficatio 而来。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its outcome.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指动作，也指结果。

items.example: It also stands behind verity and very.
items.exampleCN: 它还构成 verity 与 very。

items.example: It is the source of the -fy and -fication endings.
items.exampleCN: 它是 -fy 与 -fication 词尾的来源。

items.example: It builds classification, simplification and purification.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分类、简化与提纯等词。

items.example: It builds verify, clarify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它构成核实、澄清与放大等动词。

items.example: The adjective sets the standard for a good claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为好的主张立下标准。

items.meaning: one who or that which checks
items.example: The ending marks the person or the tool.
The abstract noun names a property rather than an act.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指属性而非动作。

latinEntries.meaning: to make true; to prove true
latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin verificare means to make true.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 verificare 意为使之为真。

latinEntries.example: Latin verus means true, and gives veracity and verdict.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 verus 意为真的，并给出 veracity 与 verdict。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb facere (fac-, factum; to make)
latinEntries.example: Latin facere means to make or do.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 facere 意为做、造。

derivatives.zh: 核实；证实
可核实的
可核实性
核验者；验证程序
已核实的
证实主义

definition_zh: 核实；证实；查证；验证（身份、数据、真伪）
definition_en: to check or prove that something is true, accurate or genuine
core_image: 一只手把证据和账本逐条核对，最后在末尾打上勾
scene: 门卫拦下访客，让他出示证件，又对着名单一个字母一个字母地核对。The guard verified her name against the list before opening the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 verify 是「核实、查证」（第 1 个义项：检查某事是否真实准确）；句意为门卫开门前对照名单核实了她的名字。逐条核对再打勾的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：核实、查证；证实；验证

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ication 构成，义为「核实；验证」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可核实的；可验证的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「已核实的；经验证的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「核实者；校验器」

senses.title: To check the facts
senses.titleCN: 核实：检查事实是否正确
senses.definition: to check that information is true or accurate
senses.definitionCN: 检查信息是否真实、准确
senses.example: Please verify the figures before the report goes out.
senses.exampleCN: 报告发布之前请核实这些数字。
senses.why: Latin verus means true and facere means to make; to verify is to make a thing true in the sense of proving it so.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 verus 意为「真」，facere 意为「做」；verify 就是通过证明来把一件事确立为真。

senses.title: To confirm with evidence
senses.definition: to establish the truth of something by presenting evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过出示证据来确立某事的真实性
senses.example: Two independent witnesses verified his account.
senses.exampleCN: 两名独立证人证实了他的说法。
senses.why: Checking becomes proving when evidence is laid beside the claim, as one pan of a balance beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 当证据被摆在说法一旁，如同天平两边相对，核对就变成了证实。

senses.title: To confirm identity
senses.titleCN: 核验身份：确认是不是本人
senses.definition: to establish that a person or document is genuine, as with a passport or password
senses.definitionCN: 确认某个人或证件真实无误，如查验护照或密码
senses.example: Banks must verify the identity of every new customer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须核验每一位新客户的身份。
senses.why: A person can be 'true' too: the same test applies to who someone is, not only to what a claim says.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是「真的」：同一套检验既用于一句话是否属实，也用于一个人是谁。

senses.title: To test a system or figure
senses.titleCN: 验证：检验数据或系统是否成立
senses.definition: to test a result, calculation or system to show that it works as claimed
senses.definitionCN: 检验结果、计算或系统是否如所称那样运行
senses.example: The engineers verified the bridge design with a computer model.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用计算机模型验证了桥梁设计。
senses.why: Here the truth under test is a working thing, and the test produces the proof.
senses.whyCN: 此时受检验的「真」是一件能运转的东西，而检验本身就产出了证明。

senses.title: As in verified accounts
senses.definition: used adjectivally in phrases such as a verified account, meaning officially confirmed
senses.definitionCN: 以形容词形式用于 verified account「已认证账号」等说法，意为经官方确认的
senses.example: Her verified account carries a small blue badge.
senses.exampleCN: 她的已认证账号上带着一个小小的蓝色标记。
senses.why: The act becomes a state: once the check is done, the mark stays on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成了状态：核对一旦完成，标记就留在那件东西上。

intro.en: Verify joins two Latin words, verus 'true' and facere 'to make', and the pair travelled through French into English.
intro.cn: verify 由两个拉丁词合成：verus「真」与 facere「做」，这一组合经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective verus meant 'true, real, genuine', and it also gave veritas 'truth'.
items.cn: 形容词 verus 意为「真的、真实的」，它还生出 veritas「真理」。

items.en: The verb facere meant 'to make, do', the source of dozens of English -fy verbs.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，是英语许多以 -fy 结尾动词的来源。

items.en: Verificare meant 'to make true, prove to be true'; the medieval form is documented, though its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: verificare 意为「使成真、证明为真」；这一中世纪形式有文献可查，但首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old French verifier carried the sense of proving or establishing a thing as true.
items.cn: 古法语 verifier 带有「证明或确立某事物为真」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed verify in the fourteenth century, first in legal and scholarly contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 verify，最初多用于法律与学术语境。

items.en: Computing gave the word a technical life: to verify data, a signature or an account.
items.cn: 计算机领域赋予这个词技术生命：验证数据、签名或账号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Latin -ficare verbs; the near-meaning group gathers ways of checking and confirming.
note.cn: 形近组收其他拉丁语 -ficare 动词；近义组收各种核对与确认的说法。

entries.definition: To make something clear; clarus 'clear' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「澄清」，由 clarus「清楚」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To confirm officially in writing; certus 'sure' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、颁发证书」，由 certus「确定」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To recognise or establish who or what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「识别、确认身份」。

entries.definition: The noun of checking that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「核实、验证」。

entries.definition: To state that something is certainly true, often after being asked.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认」，常在被询问之后表示某事确实如此。

entries.definition: To look at something quickly to see whether it is right; the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To prove something is valid or acceptable, especially by official test.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使生效、验证有效」，多指经过正式检验。

entries.definition: To support a claim with evidence; formal and heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实、用证据支持」，语气正式而厚重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real Latin parts, verus and facere, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语两部件 verus 与 facere，以及这个词出现的短语。

normal.en: veri- is true and -fy is to make: verify is to make true by proof.
normal.cn: veri- 是真，-fy 是做：verify 就是靠证明把事做真。

normal.en: Verify comes before you trust; confirm often comes when someone asks.
normal.cn: verify 发生在你相信之前；confirm 多发生在有人问起时。

normal.en: Verification is the noun, verifiable the adjective: check, then the checkable quality.
normal.cn: verification 是名词，verifiable 是形容词：先核对，再谈可核对的性质。

normal.en: A verified account has passed the check and keeps the badge.
normal.cn: 已认证账号通过了核对，于是保留那个标记。

normal.en: Computers verify a password in milliseconds; a witness may take years.
normal.cn: 计算机毫秒之间校验密码，而一个证人可能要用好几年。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: the claim on the left, the evidence on the right, and a tick when they line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上两栏：左边是说法，右边是证据，两者对齐时打一个勾。

abstract.en: The word is built to make truth, not to find it: the act of proving is what creates the certainty.
abstract.cn: 这个词生来是要「造出」真，而不是「发现」真：证明这一动作本身造出了确定。

abstract.en: The same tick works for facts, for identity and for a design that must hold a bridge.
abstract.cn: 同一个勾适用于事实、身份，以及必须撑住一座桥的设计。

examples.en: Journalists must verify a story before publishing it.
examples.cn: 记者在发表报道之前必须核实。

examples.en: The software verifies your password each time you log in.
examples.cn: 每次登录时，软件都会校验你的密码。

examples.en: Officials could not verify the number of people in the camp.
examples.cn: 官员无法核实营地中的人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「verify 为瑞发」——为瑞（veri）发一张证明，核料必须是真的：核实

root: 由拉丁语 verus「真的」与 facere「做、造」组合而成，中世纪拉丁语 verificare「证明为真」，经古法语 verifier 进入英语；同族词有 verity、verdict、clarify、certify。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of verify move from checking a fact, to proving it with evidence, to testing a person, a system, and finally the lasting mark of a passed check.
sensesIntro.cn: verify 的五个义项从核对事实，到用证据证实，再到检验一个人、一套系统，最后落在通过核验后留下的持久标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns on a page, claim and evidence, with a tick where they meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸上的两栏，说法与证据，在二者吻合处打一个勾。

branches.en: CHECK LINE: the eye runs down the list comparing each item.
branches.cn: 核对线：目光沿清单逐项比对。

branches.en: PROOF LINE: evidence is set beside the claim until the balance is level.
branches.cn: 证明线：把证据摆在说法旁边，直到天平持平。

branches.en: TEST LINE: a person or a system is put through the same test.
branches.cn: 检验线：人和系统都要经过同一套检验。

branches.en: MARK LINE: the finished check leaves a badge behind.
branches.cn: 标记线：核验完成后留下一个标记。

branches.en: CONTRAST: check looks, verify proves, confirm answers.
branches.cn: 对照线：check 是看，verify 是证明，confirm 是应声作答。

intro.en: Verify is a Latin compound: a true-root plus a make-root, closed by English endings.
intro.cn: verify 是拉丁语复合词：一个「真」词根加一个「做」词根，再以英语词尾收束。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin halves are documented: verus and facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的两半都有文献可查：verus 与 facere。

items.example: It carries the idea of truth.

items.exampleCN: 它连接 verus 与 facere。
它构成 clarify 与 certify。

definition_zh: 多才多艺的；多用途的；适应性强的；多功能的；灵活的
definition_en: able to turn to many different skills, uses or roles instead of being fixed to one
core_image: 同一个人先后站在球场三个不同位置，脚边的战术板画着三条不同的跑位线
scene: 一名球员先踢前锋，又回撤中场，最后临时顶到后防线，教练在场边不断改画战术板。The coach valued her as a versatile player who could fill three positions.
sceneCN: 这里指一个人能胜任多个位置与角色（第 1 个义项：多才多艺、能担多职）；句意为教练看重她这名能踢三个位置的多面手。图中可辨识物件：足球场、三个不同站位、不断改画的战术板。

pos.zh: 多才多艺的；多用途的；适应性强的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示性质的名词词尾构成，义为「多才多艺；多用途」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以多用途的方式」，较少使用

senses.title: Able to take many roles
senses.definition: of a person, able to perform well in several different positions or jobs
senses.definitionCN: 指一个人能在多个不同位置或工作中都表现良好
senses.example: The coach valued her as a versatile player who could fill three positions.
senses.exampleCN: 教练看重她这名能踢三个位置的多面手。
senses.why: The Latin adjective meant turning about; a person who can turn to a new role keeps that motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词意为「能转动的」；一个人能转向新角色，就保留了这种转动。

senses.title: Serving many purposes
senses.definition: of a tool or material, useful for a wide range of tasks
senses.definitionCN: 指工具或材料可用于很广的一类任务
senses.example: A versatile knife is the only tool the campers carry.
senses.exampleCN: 一把多用途小刀是露营者唯一携带的工具。
senses.why: An object cannot choose a role, yet it can be turned to many uses, which is the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 物件不会自己选角色，却能转向很多用途，这正是同一幅图景。

senses.title: Adaptable to new conditions
senses.definition: able to adjust quickly to changed demands or settings
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速适应变化了的要求或环境
senses.example: The versatile crew could work both on deck and in the engine room.
senses.exampleCN: 这支适应性强的船员队伍既能在甲板工作，也能进机舱。
senses.why: Adaptation is turning in place: the same ability meets an unfamiliar demand.
senses.whyCN: 适应就是原地转向：同一种能力去应对陌生的要求。

senses.title: Multi-function in design
senses.definition: combining several functions in one device, space or system
senses.definitionCN: 把多种功能合在一个设备、空间或系统中
senses.example: The versatile studio works as a classroom by day and a rehearsal hall by night.
senses.exampleCN: 这间多功能工作室白天当教室，晚上当排练厅。
senses.why: Architecture uses the word for a room that can be turned to a second purpose without rebuilding.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学用这个词指一间不必重建就能转向第二种用途的房间。

senses.title: Wide-ranging in style or skill
senses.definition: showing a broad range of styles or techniques rather than one narrow speciality
senses.definitionCN: 展现广泛风格或技法，而非一门狭窄专长
senses.example: Her versatile voice moved easily between folk song and jazz.
senses.exampleCN: 她多面的嗓音在民谣与爵士之间自如转换。
senses.why: The word praises range itself, not just the ability to switch tasks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词赞赏的是广度本身，而不只是能换任务。

senses.title: Useful across many jobs
senses.definition: of an employee, able to cover several functions in one organisation
senses.definitionCN: 指雇员能在一个组织里承担多项职能
senses.example: Small firms prefer versatile staff who can cover two desks.
senses.exampleCN: 小公司偏爱能顶两个岗位的多面手员工。
senses.why: Employment turns versatility into an economic asset: fewer people, more roles.
senses.whyCN: 雇佣关系把「多面」变成经济资产：更少的人，更多的角色。

senses.title: Flexible in layout or use
senses.definition: of a space or plan, open to more than one arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 指空间或方案可以容纳不止一种安排
senses.example: The versatile floor plan allowed the tenants to combine two units.
senses.exampleCN: 灵活的平面布局让租户可以把两个单元合并。
senses.why: The turning is now spatial: walls and uses can be rearranged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的转动是空间性的：墙体与用途都可以重新排列。

senses.title: Able to think along many lines
senses.titleCN: 思路灵活、能多角度思考
senses.definition: of a mind, able to approach a problem from several directions
senses.definitionCN: 指头脑能从多个方向接近一个问题
senses.example: A versatile thinker is hard to surprise in a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 思路灵活的人在辩论中很难被出其不意。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: what turns is not the body but the line of thought.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：转动的不是身体，而是思路。

senses.title: An all-round athlete
senses.definition: of an athlete, competitive across several events or disciplines
senses.definitionCN: 指运动员能在多个项目或分项中竞争
senses.example: The versatile gymnast qualified for four different finals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位全能型体操选手晋级了四个不同的决赛。
senses.why: Sport gives versatility a scoreboard: the all-rounder is measured across events.
senses.whyCN: 体育给「多面」配了记分牌：全能选手跨项目被测量。

intro.en: Versatile is a Latin adjective for something that turns, from a verb meaning to keep turning; English extended the image from objects to people and skills.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「会转动的」形容词，来自意为「不断转动」的动词；英语把这一意象从物件扩展到人与技能。

items.en: vertere meant to turn, to turn around, and it is the root of version, convert and many more.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转、使转向」，是 version、convert 等许多词的词根。

items.en: versare was a frequentative form, suggesting repeated or restless turning.
items.cn: versare 是反复态形式，暗示反复或不停地转动。

items.en: versatilis described a thing that can be turned about, hence adaptable.
items.cn: versatilis 描述可以被转来转去的东西，因此引申为「可适应的」。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English in the sixteenth century; the earliest records are approximate in date but the source line is clear.
items.cn: 法语在十六世纪把这个形容词传给英语；最早记录的具体年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: English extended a word about turning objects to people who can turn to many skills.
items.cn: 英语把原本描述物体转动的词，扩展用于能转向多种技能的人。

items.en: Design and sport now use the adjective for multi-function rooms and all-round athletes.
items.cn: 设计与体育如今用这个形容词指多功能空间与全能运动员。

note.en: The first group shares the turning root or looks close; the second group names nearby kinds of flexibility. Note the double layer: versatile describes both a person with many skills and an object with many uses, and the near words usually cover only one of those layers.
note.cn: 第一组共享「转动」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的灵活类说法。注意双层：versatile 既指人有多种本领，也指物有多种用途，而邻近词通常只覆盖其中一层。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of serving many purposes or roles.
entries.definitionCN: 指多用途或多角色的性质。

entries.definition: Skilled or experienced in a subject; it comes from the same turning verb but stresses training.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通或熟悉某领域；同一「转动」动词而来，但强调训练有素。

entries.definition: One form of something that has been turned or translated.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物经过转写或翻译后的一种形式。

entries.definition: To turn something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物转成另一种形式或用途。

entries.definition: Easily changing or evaporating; it looks close but comes from a flying root, not a turning one.
entries.definitionCN: 指易变或易挥发；形近，但来自「飞」的词根，而非「转」。

entries.definition: Standing upright; it shares the turning root through the idea of a turning point or summit.
entries.definitionCN: 指垂直的；经由「转向点、顶点」的概念共享同一词根。

entries.definition: Able to change to fit new conditions; it stresses adjustment rather than range of uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指能改变以适应新条件；强调调整，而非用途之广。

entries.definition: Able to bend or be changed without breaking; it stresses elasticity and willingness to adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 指能弯曲或改变而不折断；强调弹性与愿意变通。

entries.definition: Good at many things rather than specialising; it is warmer and more colloquial for people.
entries.definitionCN: 指多方面都好而不专精；用于人时更亲切、更口语。

entries.definition: Having many sides or aspects; it describes complexity rather than practical use.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有许多侧面或面向；描述复杂性，而非实用多能。

entries.definition: Designed for several uses; it covers the object layer of versatile but says nothing about a person's skills.
entries.definitionCN: 指为多种用途设计；只覆盖本词的「物」这一层，不涉及人的本领。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin turning image, the real object and person pairs, and the real contrast with volatile.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「转动」意象、真实的物件与人的双重用法，以及与 volatile 的真实区别。

normal.en: The root means turn: a versatile person can turn from one role to another without losing balance.
normal.cn: 词根意为「转」：多才多艺的人能从一种角色转到另一种，而不失衡。

normal.en: The same adjective fits a knife with many blades and a player with many positions.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既适合多刀口的小刀，也适合能踢多个位置的球员。

normal.en: Versatile player, versatile tool and versatile material are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 多面手球员、多用途工具与多用途材料是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Versatility is the noun; turn the adjective into a quality and you have it.
normal.cn: versatility 是名词；把形容词变成一种性质就得到它。

normal.en: Do not confuse turning with flying: volatile is the word built on flight.
normal.cn: 别把「转」和「飞」混了：volatile 是建立在「飞行」上的词。

abstract.en: Versatility is not knowing everything; it is refusing to be only one thing.
abstract.cn: 多才多艺不是无所不知，而是拒绝只做一样东西。

abstract.en: A tool with many uses is also a tool with no single identity, which is both its freedom and its cost.
abstract.cn: 多用途的工具也是没有单一身份的工具，这既是自由，也是代价。

abstract.en: The turning image suggests balance: turn too far and the versatile becomes merely scattered.
abstract.cn: 转动的意象暗示平衡：转得太远，多面就变成了散乱。

examples.en: The workshop needs a versatile technician who can handle both wiring and plumbing.
examples.cn: 车间需要一名既能处理电路又能处理水管的万能技师。

examples.en: Bamboo is a versatile material for furniture, scaffolding and paper.
examples.cn: 竹子是可用于家具、脚手架和纸张的多用途材料。

examples.en: Her versatile style made her the obvious choice for the opening act.
examples.cn: 她多面的风格使她成为开场表演的当然人选。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛赛头」——能转来转去，样样都能上手

root: 来自拉丁语 versatilis「可转动的、可变通的」← versare「反复转动」← vertere「转」，经法语于十六世纪进入英语。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a person with many roles through tools, adaptation, design, style, employment, space and thought to an all-round athlete.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从能担多职的人，经过工具、适应、设计、风格、雇佣、空间与思维，最后落到全能运动员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one body stands in three different positions on the same pitch, each with its own line of movement.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一具身体在同一片球场上站过三个位置，每个位置都有各自的跑动线。

branches.en: THE PERSON: roles, styles and events that one performer can cover.
branches.cn: 人：一个表演者能覆盖的角色、风格与项目。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a tool or a room turned to more than one purpose.
branches.cn: 物：被转向不止一种用途的工具或房间。

branches.en: THE WORKING LIFE: a crew or employee who adapts to new demands.
branches.cn: 工作生涯：适应新要求的班组或员工。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a layout open to more than one arrangement.
branches.cn: 方案：可容纳不止一种安排的布局。

branches.en: THE MIND: a line of thought that can turn to another angle.
branches.cn: 心智：能转向另一角度的思路。

intro.en: Versatile is a Latin turning verb plus an adjective ending meaning able to be.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁「转动」动词加一个表示「能被……的」形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vertere, versare and versatilis; the English noun versatility adds a quality ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vertere、versare 与 versatilis；英语名词 versatility 再加一个性质词尾。

items.exampleCN: 反复态形式加上持续运动。
这个形容词意为「可适应的」。

items.example: The borrowed adjective keeps the motion.
items.exampleCN: 借入的形容词保留运动。

items.example: It forms versatilely, a rare adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较少用的副词 versatilely。

items.example: The same root gives the facing word.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根给出表示「相对」的词。

items.example: A sister word keeps the turning.

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加性质名词词尾构成，义为「多才多艺」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以多用途方式」

definition_zh: 版本；说法、描述；（软件、文件的）修订本；改编本
definition_en: a particular form of something that differs from other forms of it, such as a copy, an account, or an edition
core_image: 同一份稿子被改了又改，桌上摊着好几份，每一份都略有不同
scene: 编辑把同一篇文章的三个版本并排打开，逐段比较。The final version was shorter than the first one by two pages.
sceneCN: 这里 version 是「版本」（第 1 个义项：与同一事物的其他形式不同的某个形态）；句意为最终版本比第一版短了两页。几份稿子并排放在桌上，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：版本；说法；改编本；译文

collocations.phrase: a film version of the novel

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀构成，义为「与版本有关的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「版本管理、版本化」
同一拉丁词根 vert-「转」构成，义为「多才多艺的；多用途的」
同一词根构成，义为「转换；改变信仰」

senses.title: One form among many
senses.titleCN: 版本：众多形态中的一种
senses.definition: a particular form of something, in which it differs from other forms of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的一种特定形态，与其他形态有所差别
senses.example: The paper published a longer version of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了那次访谈的较长版本。
senses.why: Latin vertere means to turn; a version is the same matter turned a little differently.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertere 意为「转」；version 就是同一件事被稍稍转了个角度。

senses.title: One person's account
senses.titleCN: 说法：某人对事情的一种讲法
senses.definition: one person's account of an event, especially when others may tell it differently
senses.definitionCN: 某人对一件事的讲述，尤指他人可能有不同讲法时
senses.example: The two witnesses gave very different versions of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人对事故的说法大相径庭。
senses.why: An account is also a turning: the same event passes through one perspective and comes out shaped by it.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是一种转动：同一件事经过一个人的视角，出来时已被这个视角塑形。

senses.title: An edition or revision
senses.titleCN: 修订本：经过修改的一版
senses.definition: a revised or updated edition of a text, file or product
senses.definitionCN: 文本、文件或产品经过修改更新的一个版本
senses.example: This is the third version of the manual, and it is much clearer.
senses.exampleCN: 这是手册的第三版，清楚多了。
senses.why: Each revision turns the draft once more, and the newest turn is what users install.
senses.whyCN: 每一次修订都把稿子再转一次，最新的那一转就是用户安装的那个。

senses.title: An adaptation
senses.titleCN: 改编本：由原作改成的形式
senses.definition: a form of a work that has been adapted for another medium or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为另一种媒介或受众改编而成的作品形式
senses.example: The film version leaves out the youngest brother entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编版把最小的弟弟整个删掉了。
senses.why: Moving a story to the screen is a literal turning: the same characters now seen from a new side.
senses.whyCN: 把故事搬上银幕是一种字面意义上的转动：同一些人物从新的方向被看见。

senses.title: A specific release of software
senses.titleCN: 软件的一个具体发行版
senses.definition: a numbered release of a program or document, used to track changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 带编号的程序或文档发行版本，用于追踪变化
senses.example: Please update to version 4.2 before sending the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件之前请更新到 4.2 版。
senses.why: In modern use the turning is numbered: each fix produces one more version on the record.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法里，这种转动被编了号：每修一处，记录上就多一个版本。

intro.en: Version comes from the Latin verb 'to turn', and the whole family follows that image of turning.
intro.cn: version 源自拉丁语表示「转」的动词，整个词族都沿着这一转动的意象展开。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn, turn around, change'; it lies behind convert, revert and reverse.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转、回转、改变」，它是 convert、revert、reverse 背后的词。

items.en: Versio meant 'a turning, a change, a translation'; the noun names the act of turning something.
items.cn: versio 意为「转动、改变、翻译」，这一名词指把某物转一次这件事。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word for a translation or rendering of a text.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个词，指文本的翻译或转写。

items.en: English adopted version first for translations, then for any form differing from another.
items.cn: 英语最初用 version 指译本，后来泛指与其他形式有别的任一形态。

items.en: Publishing, then computing, turned it into a counting word: first version, final version, version number.
items.cn: 出版业再到计算机业把它变成计数词：第一版、最终版、版本号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin turn-root; the near-meaning group gathers words for forms and accounts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「转」词根构成的词；近义组收表示形态与说法的词。

entries.definition: The act of turning something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转换、转变」，指把某物变成另一形态或用途。

entries.definition: To turn the other way round; the opposite direction of the same turn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颠倒、反转」，是同一转动的相反方向。

entries.definition: Turned apart, hence different; a family voice of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，本义为「转向不同方向」。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多才多艺的、多用途的」，即能转向许多用途。

entries.definition: One printing or published form of a text, usually revised.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版次」，指文本的一次印行，通常经过修订。

entries.definition: A report or description of what happened; the everyday word for sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、说法」，是义项 02 的日常词。

entries.definition: A form that differs slightly, often in spelling or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，指略有差别的形式，多指拼写或措辞。

entries.definition: A performance or translation of a work, stressing the performer's version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演绎、译文」，强调表演者或译者的处理。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb vertere and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 vertere，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: version shares its root with turn: each version is the same thing turned again.
normal.cn: version 与 turn 同根：每个版本都是同一件东西又转过一次。

normal.en: Different witnesses, different versions: the same event turned through different eyes.
normal.cn: 不同的证人给出不同的说法：同一件事经过不同的眼睛转动一次。

normal.en: Software asks for a version number; a novel asks for a film version.
normal.cn: 软件要的是版本号；小说要的是电影改编版。

normal.en: The original version stays the reference while later versions move away from it.
normal.cn: 原版始终是参照，后来的版本则离它越来越远。

normal.en: Ver- inside version echoes vertere, the turning verb of Latin.
normal.cn: version 里的 ver- 呼应 vertere，即拉丁语那个「转」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture one sheet of paper on a turntable: each small rotation shows a slightly different face, and each face is a version.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸放在转盘上：每一次微转都露出略不同的正面，每一面都是一个版本。

abstract.en: A version is never the thing itself, only a way of seeing it, which is why accounts can disagree.
abstract.cn: 版本从来不是事物本身，只是一种看它的方式，所以各种说法可以彼此矛盾。

abstract.en: The word travels from clay tablets to code without changing its logic: turn, compare, number.
abstract.cn: 这个词从泥板一路走到代码，逻辑却没变：转动、比较、编号。

examples.en: This is an older version of the map, without the new road.
examples.cn: 这是这幅地图的旧版本，上面还没有那条新路。

examples.en: Each witness told a slightly different version of the night.
examples.cn: 每个证人对那一夜的讲述都略有不同。

examples.en: The app will not open until you install the latest version.
examples.cn: 不安装最新版本，这个应用就打不开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）想（sion）」——同一个故事，我想的说法和别人不一样：版本

root: 源自拉丁语 versio「转动、翻译」，来自动词 vertere「转」；经古法语进入英语；同族词有 convert、reverse、diverse、versatile。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of version all rest on one turning: the same matter presented in another form, as an account, an edition, an adaptation, or a numbered release.
sensesIntro.cn: version 的五个义项都建立在一次转之上：同一件事以另一种形态出现，或是说法、或是修订本、或是改编、或是编号发行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of one article side by side on a desk, each slightly changed.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一篇文章的几份稿子并排在桌上，每份都略有变化。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the noun names any one form of many.
branches.cn: 形态线：名词指众多形态中的任意一种。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: an account is the event turned through one person.
branches.cn: 说法线：说法就是事件经过某个人转动后的样子。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: editions and software releases are numbered turns.
branches.cn: 计数线：版本与软件发行都是被编号的一次转动。

branches.en: MEDIUM LINE: the story turns from page to screen.
branches.cn: 媒介线：故事从纸面转到银幕。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the original is the point from which every version departs.
branches.cn: 对照线：原版是所有版本由之离开的那个点。

intro.en: Version is a Latin noun stem with an English noun ending; the turning root stays visible inside it.
intro.cn: version 是拉丁语名词词干加英语名词词尾，其中的「转」词根仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertere, with the noun versio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：动词 vertere 及其名词 versio。

items.example: It forms version from the stem.

definition_zh: 脊椎动物；有脊椎的
definition_en: an animal with a backbone, or having a backbone
core_image: 一条完整的脊柱从颅骨延伸到尾端，一节节椎骨串成不间断的链
scene: 解剖台上，一只小动物的脊柱被完整取出，一节节椎骨从颅骨一直串到尾端。 The vertebrate spine ran from skull to tail in one unbroken chain of bones.
sceneCN: 这里 vertebrate 指「脊椎动物的」（第 1 个义项：有脊柱的动物），在此作定语；句意为这只脊椎动物的脊柱从颅骨到尾端串成一条不间断的骨链。

pos.zh: 脊椎动物
有脊椎的

derivatives.zh: 脊椎动物（复数）
脊椎动物亚门（分类名）
脊椎动物古生物学
无脊椎动物；无脊椎的

senses.title: An animal with a backbone
senses.definition: any animal with a vertebral column, including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals
senses.definitionCN: 任何有脊柱的动物，包括鱼、两栖动物、爬行动物、鸟类与哺乳动物
senses.example: The vertebrate spine ran from skull to tail in one chain.
senses.exampleCN: 这只脊椎动物的脊柱从颅骨到尾端串成一条链。
senses.why: The word is built directly on vertebra, the bones that make up the spine, so the backbone is the defining trait.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接建立在 vertebra（构成脊柱的骨节）之上，因此脊柱就是定义特征。

senses.title: The adjective: having a backbone
senses.definition: describing an animal or structure that possesses a spinal column
senses.definitionCN: 描述拥有脊柱的动物或结构
senses.example: The vertebrate body plan includes a skull and a closed circulatory system.
senses.exampleCN: 脊椎动物的身体结构包括颅骨与闭锁式循环系统。
senses.why: As with invertebrate, noun and adjective share one form, so the same word can modify another noun.
senses.whyCN: 与 invertebrate 一样，名词和形容词同形，因此同一个词可以修饰另一个名词。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的脊椎动物类群
senses.definition: the vertebrates collectively, a subphylum of the chordates
senses.definitionCN: 所有脊椎动物的集合，是脊索动物门下的一个亚门
senses.example: Vertebrates are a small fraction of all animal species.
senses.exampleCN: 脊椎动物只占全部动物物种的一小部分。
senses.why: Although familiar, the group is numerically small, and the plural is used for the category rather than for a herd.
senses.whyCN: 这一类群虽为人熟悉，数量却很少，因此复数形式指的是范畴，而不是一群个体。

senses.title: The subject of vertebrate palaeontology
senses.titleCN: 脊椎动物古生物学的研究对象
senses.definition: fossil vertebrates, studied for evidence of evolution and past environments
senses.definitionCN: 化石脊椎动物，用于研究演化与古环境
senses.example: Vertebrate fossils in the badlands trace the rise of mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 荒地上的脊椎动物化石记录了哺乳动物的兴起。
senses.why: The field needs the adjective because it studies bones and teeth, which are vertebrate specialities.
senses.whyCN: 这一领域需要这个形容词，因为它研究骨骼与牙齿，而这是脊椎动物的特长。

senses.title: A laboratory model animal
senses.definition: a vertebrate used in research, such as a mouse or zebrafish
senses.definitionCN: 用于研究的脊椎动物，如小鼠或斑马鱼
senses.example: The mouse is the standard vertebrate model for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 小鼠是遗传学的标准脊椎动物模型。
senses.why: Medical research contrasts vertebrate models with invertebrate ones, and the adjective marks that distinction.
senses.whyCN: 医学研究把脊椎动物模型与无脊椎动物模型相对照，这个形容词正标出这一区别。

senses.title: A surveyed vertebrate fauna
senses.titleCN: 调查所得的脊椎动物群
senses.definition: the vertebrate species recorded in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区记录到的脊椎动物物种
senses.example: The vertebrate fauna of the island includes no large predators.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的脊椎动物群中没有大型捕食者。
senses.why: Surveys separate vertebrate from invertebrate records because the methods and expertise differ.
senses.whyCN: 调查把脊椎动物与无脊椎动物记录分开，因为方法与专业不同。

senses.title: A vertebrate pest
senses.definition: a vertebrate that damages crops, property or ecosystems, such as a rodent
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物、财产或生态系统的脊椎动物，如啮齿类
senses.example: Rodent control targets vertebrate pests rather than insects.
senses.exampleCN: 鼠类防治针对的是脊椎动物有害生物，而不是昆虫。
senses.why: Pest management uses the category to separate rodent and bird problems from insect problems.
senses.whyCN: 有害生物管理用这一范畴把鼠类与鸟类问题同昆虫问题分开。

senses.title: A conservation unit
senses.definition: a vertebrate species or population managed for conservation
senses.definitionCN: 为保护而管理的脊椎动物物种或种群
senses.example: The park monitors vertebrate populations every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 公园每年春天监测脊椎动物种群。
senses.why: Conservation reporting often counts vertebrates because they are large, visible and easy to survey.
senses.whyCN: 保护报告常统计脊椎动物，因为它们体型大、可见、易于调查。

intro.en: Vertebrate is Latin vertebra 'spinal joint' plus the adjective ending -ate; zoology adopted it as a group name in the modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vertebrate 由拉丁 vertebra「脊椎关节」加形容词词尾 -ate 构成；动物学在近代把它采用为类群名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertebra meant 'joint', especially a joint of the spine, from vertere 'to turn'. The connection with turning is generally accepted; the earlier root is reconstructed.
items.cn: vertebra 意为「关节」，尤指脊柱关节，来自 vertere「转动」。与「转动」的联系一般被接受；更早的词根属重构。

items.en: Vertebratus meant 'jointed, provided with vertebrae', an adjective formed from the noun, and it supplied the shape of the English word.
items.cn: vertebratus 意为「有关节的、具椎骨的」，是由名词构成的形容词，提供了英语词的形态。

items.en: Lamarck's classification used vertébrés for backboned animals in the early nineteenth century, pairing it with invertébrés.
items.cn: 拉马克在 19 世纪初的分类中用 vertébrés 指有脊柱的动物，与 invertébrés 相对。

items.en: English vertebrate appears in the nineteenth century as noun and adjective, first in zoological and anatomical writing.
items.cn: 英语 vertebrate 在 19 世纪出现，兼作名词与形容词，最初见于动物学与解剖学文字。

items.en: Vertebrate palaeontology became a distinct field as fossil bones and teeth were catalogued separately from shelled invertebrates.
items.cn: 随着化石骨骼与牙齿同带壳的无脊椎动物分开编目，脊椎动物古生物学成为独立领域。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Latin stages are clear, but the pre-Latin root of vertere is reconstructed and the exact first English citation is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：拉丁阶段清楚，但 vertere 的拉丁语之前词根属重构，英语确切首见书证也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the vertebra family that are easily swapped; group two holds broader or neighbouring animal categories.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 vertebra 词族、容易混用的词；第二组是更宽或相邻的动物范畴。

entries.definition: An animal without a backbone; the only difference is the prefix in-, which reverses the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 没有脊柱的动物；唯一差别是否定前缀 in-，意义正好相反。

entries.definition: A single spinal bone; the animal word is built on it, but the bone is not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 单块脊椎骨；动物词由它构成，但骨不等于动物。

entries.definition: Relating to vertebrae or the spine, as in vertebral column; it does not name an animal group.
entries.definitionCN: 与椎骨或脊柱有关，如 vertebral column；它不指动物类群。

entries.definition: The formal Latin name of the group; Vertebrata is the whole subphylum, vertebrate is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 该群的正式拉丁名；Vertebrata 是整个亚门，vertebrate 是其中一个成员。

entries.definition: Any animal with a notochord at some stage, including vertebrates and some invertebrates; it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 任何在某一阶段具脊索的动物，包括脊椎动物与部分无脊椎动物；范围更宽。

entries.definition: A vertebrate with four limbs, such as a mammal, bird or reptile; fish are vertebrates but not tetrapods.
entries.definitionCN: 有四肢的脊椎动物，如哺乳动物、鸟或爬行动物；鱼是脊椎动物但不是四足动物。

entries.definition: A warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young milk; mammals are one class within Vertebrata.
entries.definitionCN: 以乳汁哺育幼崽的温血脊椎动物；哺乳动物是脊椎动物亚门中的一个纲。

entries.definition: An animal with a skull, essentially synonymous with vertebrate in modern usage but defined by the head shield.
entries.definitionCN: 有颅骨的动物，现代用法中基本与脊椎动物同义，但定义依据是头骨。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Vertebra is the bone; vertebrate is the animal that has a chain of them.
normal.cn: vertebra 是骨头；vertebrate 是拥有这一串骨头的动物。

normal.en: Fish, frogs, snakes, birds and mice are all vertebrates; insects and crabs are not.
normal.cn: 鱼、蛙、蛇、鸟、鼠都是脊椎动物；昆虫与蟹不是。

normal.en: The negative prefix in- turns vertebrate into its opposite, invertebrate.
normal.cn: 否定前缀 in- 把 vertebrate 变成反义词 invertebrate。

normal.en: Vertebrate palaeontology studies bones and teeth; invertebrate palaeontology studies shells.
normal.cn: 脊椎动物古生物学研究骨骼与牙齿；无脊椎动物古生物学研究贝壳。

normal.en: Vertebrata is the subphylum; vertebrate is one member.
normal.cn: Vertebrata 是亚门；vertebrate 是一个成员。

abstract.en: Picture a rope of bone running from head to tail, holding the whole body together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从头顶贯到尾端的骨绳，把整个身体串起来。

abstract.en: Picture a museum hall where teeth and bones tell a story shells cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一座博物馆大厅，牙齿与骨骼讲述着贝壳讲不出的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a mouse in a lab standing in for the whole vertebrate line.
abstract.cn: 想象实验室里一只小鼠，代表整条脊椎动物演化线。

examples.en: Only about five per cent of described animal species are vertebrates.
examples.cn: 已描述的动物物种中只有约百分之五为脊椎动物。

examples.en: The vertebrate fossil record begins in the Cambrian seas.
examples.cn: 脊椎动物的化石记录始于寒武纪海洋。

examples.en: Vertebrate pests such as rats damage both crops and stored grain.
examples.cn: 鼠类等脊椎动物有害生物既损害作物也损害仓储谷物。

dict_mnemonic.text: vertebra（椎骨）+ ate——身上有一串椎骨的动物，就是脊椎动物；记「有脊梁的才算」

root: 拉丁 vertebra「脊椎关节」（源自 vertere「转动」）+ -ate；vertebra 的更深词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one backbone through zoology, palaeontology, laboratory work, field surveys, pest control and conservation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一条脊柱穿过动物学、古生物学、实验室工作、野外调查、有害生物防治与保护工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of vertebrae running from skull to tail without a break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串椎骨从颅骨连到尾端，中间没有断开。

branches.en: THE SPINE: noun and adjective both rest on the presence of vertebrae.
branches.cn: 脊柱：名词与形容词都建立在「有椎骨」这一点上。

branches.en: A SMALL, FAMILIAR GROUP: numerous as individuals, few as species.
branches.cn: 小而熟悉的类群：个体多，物种少。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: bones and teeth carry the vertebrate fossil record.
branches.cn: 深时：骨骼与牙齿承载着脊椎动物的化石记录。

branches.en: EXPERIMENT: a mouse or fish stands in for the whole subphylum.
branches.cn: 实验：一只小鼠或一条鱼代表整个亚门。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: survey it, control it, or protect it.
branches.cn: 管理：调查它、防治它，或保护它。

intro.en: Vertebrate is a noun-derived adjective in -ate, with a negative twin in in- and a formal group name in Vertebrata.
intro.cn: vertebrate 是由名词派生的 -ate 形容词，有 in- 构成的否定孪生词，也有正式类群名 Vertebrata。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertebra 'joint' comes from vertere 'to turn'; vertebratus is the adjective, and Vertebrata is the modern group name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vertebra「关节」来自 vertere「转动」；vertebratus 是形容词，Vertebrata 是近代类群名。

items.example: Each vertebra is a separate bone.
items.exampleCN: 每块椎骨都是独立的骨。

items.example: The ending turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成形容词。

items.example: A vertebrate has a spinal column.

items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物在数量上不及无脊椎动物。
脊椎动物亚门属于脊索动物。

items.example: The vertebral column is the backbone.

definition_zh: 垂直的；竖的；纵向的；名词：垂直线、垂直方向
definition_en: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the flat ground or to a horizontal line
core_image: 一根铅垂线从屋檐垂下，线与地面严格成直角
scene: 木匠把线坠挂在刚起的墙边，眯眼一看，线垂得笔直。The wall was not vertical, and the whole frame had to be reset.
sceneCN: 这里 vertical 是「垂直的」（第 1 个义项：与地面成直角、竖直向上向下）；句意为墙不垂直，整个框架都得重做。沿墙面垂下的铅垂线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：垂直的；竖式的；纵向的
名词：垂直线；垂直面

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「垂直地；竖直地」
加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「垂直性；竖直程度」
同源自拉丁语 vertex「顶点」，义为「顶点；最高点」
加动词后缀构成，义为「使垂直；使纵向化」

senses.title: Straight up and down
senses.definition: going straight up and down, at a right angle to the horizontal
senses.definitionCN: 笔直向上向下，与水平面成直角
senses.example: A vertical line joins the top of the page to the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 一条垂直线把页面顶部和底部连起来。
senses.why: Latin vertex means the top or the turning point at the crown; the vertical is the direction that points to the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertex 指头顶的顶点或转点；vertical 就是指向头顶的那个方向。

senses.title: Of an axis or graph
senses.titleCN: 纵轴的：图表中上下方向
senses.definition: relating to the axis that runs up and down on a graph
senses.definitionCN: 指图表中上下延伸的那一条轴
senses.example: Temperature is shown on the vertical axis of the chart.
