senses.exampleCN: 图表的纵轴表示温度。
senses.why: On paper the ground is the horizontal, so height must be stacked upward along the other axis.
senses.whyCN: 在纸面上地面是水平线，高度就只能沿着另一条轴向上堆叠。

senses.title: Of a structure's shape
senses.titleCN: 竖立的：形容建筑或结构的形态
senses.definition: standing upright rather than lying flat, as of a wall, cliff or column
senses.definitionCN: 指墙、崖壁、柱子等立起而非平躺的形态
senses.example: The climbers faced a vertical wall of wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 攀登者面对的是湿滑岩壁的垂直面。
senses.why: The abstract direction becomes a physical surface; to climb it is to go up the same line.
senses.whyCN: 抽象方向变成了实体的面；攀爬它就是沿着同一条线往上走。

senses.title: Of organisation or movement
senses.titleCN: 纵向的：组织层级或垂直起降
senses.definition: describing organisation or motion that works up and down a hierarchy, or straight up into the air
senses.definitionCN: 形容沿层级上下运作的组织方式，或笔直向上的运动
senses.example: The plane can make a vertical take-off from the narrow deck.
senses.exampleCN: 这种飞机能从狭窄的甲板上垂直起飞。
senses.why: The same geometric line now describes power and motion: straight up, with no sideways step.
senses.whyCN: 同一条几何线此时描述权力与运动：笔直向上，不向旁侧迈步。

senses.title: The noun: the upright direction
senses.titleCN: 名词：垂直方向或垂直线
senses.definition: used as a noun for a vertical line, surface or position
senses.definitionCN: 作名词使用，指垂直线、垂直面或竖直位置
senses.example: The shelf rests exactly on the vertical.
senses.exampleCN: 架子正好贴着垂直线安放。
senses.why: The adjective steps into noun use, as English often lets it: the upright itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词用法，英语常常如此：指竖直本身。

intro.en: Vertical comes from Latin vertex, the crown of the head or the top point, which itself grew from the verb 'to turn'.
intro.cn: vertical 源自拉丁语 vertex，指头顶的旋或顶点，而后者又出自表示「转」的动词。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn'; a vertex is the point where something turns or peaks.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转」；vertex 就是事物转向或达到顶点的那一点。

items.en: Vertex meant 'whirlpool, crown of the head, summit, highest point'.
items.cn: vertex 意为「漩涡、头顶的旋、顶点、最高处」。

items.en: Late Latin verticalis meant 'of the highest point', and by extension 'overhead'.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 verticalis 意为「顶点的」，引申为「正上方的」。

items.en: Astronomers used the vertical for the line straight overhead; the exact first use in this sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 天文学家借用 vertical 表示正上方的直线；这一义项的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Geometry fixed the modern sense: perpendicular to the horizon, the opposite of horizontal.
items.cn: 几何学确立了现代义：与地平线成直角，与 horizontal 相对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same vert- turning root; the near-meaning group gathers upright and perpendicular words.
note.cn: 形近组收同带 vert- 转根的词；近义组收表示竖直与垂直的词。

entries.definition: The top point or the corner where two lines meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顶点」，指最高点或两条线相交的角点。

entries.definition: Lying flat, parallel to the horizon; the partner word that frames vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「水平的」，与 vertical 相对而彼此定义。

entries.definition: Moral goodness; a different Latin word, easily confused in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美德」，来自另一个拉丁词，拼写相近容易混。

entries.definition: Standing straight up; plainer and more physical than vertical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「竖直的、站直的」，比 vertical 更朴素、更具体。

entries.definition: Meeting a line or surface at a right angle; geometric and precise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的、成直角的」，更具几何精确性。

entries.definition: Exactly vertical, as checked with a weighted line.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「垂直的」，特指用铅垂线测得笔直。

entries.definition: Rising sharply, but not necessarily straight up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡的」，形容坡面很斜，但未必竖直。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vertex and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vertex，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: vertical pairs with horizontal: one stands, the other lies flat.
normal.cn: vertical 与 horizontal 相对：一个立着，一个平躺。

normal.en: vertex is the top of the head; vertical is the line that points there.
normal.cn: vertex 是头顶的旋；vertical 就是指向那里的那条线。

normal.en: On a chart, the vertical axis shows height and the horizontal shows time.
normal.cn: 在图表上，纵轴表示高度，横轴表示时间。

normal.en: Vertical take-off means up, straight up, without a runway.
normal.cn: vertical take-off 意为不靠跑道、笔直向上起飞。

normal.en: A plumb line hangs to tell you whether a wall is truly vertical.
normal.cn: 铅垂线垂下来，用来判断墙是否真正垂直。

abstract.en: Picture a weighted string hanging beside a new brick wall; the wall is right only when it hugs the string.
abstract.cn: 想象一条挂着重物的线在新砌的砖墙旁垂下；墙只有贴着这条线才是正的。

abstract.en: The word is defined by contrast: nothing is vertical alone, only against something level.
abstract.cn: 这个词靠对比来定义：没有东西能独自垂直，只能相对于某个水平面。

abstract.en: The same line runs through geometry, buildings and graphs: up is one direction only.
abstract.cn: 同一条线贯穿几何、建筑和图表：向上的方向只有一个。

examples.en: Draw a vertical line down the middle of the page.
examples.cn: 在页面中央画一条垂直线。

examples.en: The cliff is almost vertical for the last hundred metres.
examples.cn: 最后一百米，那面崖壁几乎完全垂直。

examples.en: The vertical axis shows the number of visitors each month.
examples.cn: 纵轴表示每个月的游客人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）提（ti）抠（cal）」——我提着一根线往下抠，看墙正不正：垂直的

root: 源自拉丁语 vertex「头顶的旋、顶点」，出自动词 vertere「转」，晚期拉丁语 verticalis「顶点的」；经科学拉丁语进入英语；同族词有 vertex、convert、version。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vertical hold one line upright: a geometric direction, a graph axis, a standing surface, an upward movement, and finally the upright itself as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: vertical 的五个义项守着同一条竖直的线：几何方向、图表轴、立起的表面、向上的运动，最后是作为名词的「竖直」本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plumb line hangs beside a fresh wall, and the wall is right only if it hugs the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：铅垂线在新墙旁垂下，墙贴着这条线才算正。

branches.en: GEOMETRY LINE: straight up and down, at a right angle to the ground.
branches.cn: 几何线：笔直上下，与地面成直角。

branches.en: GRAPH LINE: the height axis of a chart.
branches.cn: 图表线：图表中的高度轴。

branches.en: SURFACE LINE: walls and cliffs that stand up to be climbed.
branches.cn: 表面线：立起来可以攀爬的墙与崖壁。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: lifting straight up, or power moving up and down a hierarchy.
branches.cn: 运动线：笔直向上升起，或权力沿层级上下运行。

branches.en: NOUN LINE: the upright itself, used as a thing.
branches.cn: 名词线：竖直本身被当作一个事物来用。

intro.en: Vertical is a Latin adjective stem with an English -al ending, built on the turning root vert-.
intro.cn: vertical 是拉丁语形容词词干接英语 -al 词尾，建立在「转」这个词根 vert- 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertex and verticalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vertex 与 verticalis。

items.example: It forms the paired word horizontal.
It forms verticals in technical use.
items.exampleCN: 它在技术语境中构成 verticals。

definition_zh: 船、舰；容器、器皿；（体内的）血管、导管
definition_en: a ship or large boat, a hollow container for liquid, or a tube that carries blood or other fluid in the body
core_image: 一个中空的器皿，能装水，也能载人渡海
scene: 港湾里停着一艘旧货船，甲板上的木桶正被吊下船。A small vessel carried the crew back to the shore at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 vessel 是「船、舰」（第 1 个义项：水上交通运输工具）；句意为黄昏时一艘小船把船员送回岸边。水上能载人的那个容器，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：船、舰；容器、器皿；血管、导管

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「有容器的；装了器皿的」（罕见）
同一拉丁词源 vas 的后代，义为「花瓶」
拉丁语原词，义为「容器」，是解剖学 vas deferens 的第一部分

senses.title: A ship or large boat
senses.titleCN: 船、舰：水上往来的大型运载工具
senses.definition: a ship or large boat, especially one used for trade or war
senses.definitionCN: 船或大型艇，尤指用于贸易或军事的
senses.example: A cargo vessel left the port before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，一艘货船就离港了。
senses.why: Latin vas means a container; a ship is the container people live in while crossing water.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vas 意为「容器」；船就是人们渡水时居住其中的那个容器。

senses.title: A container for liquid
senses.definition: a hollow container, especially one used for holding liquids
senses.definitionCN: 中空的容器，尤指盛放液体的器皿
senses.example: The priest poured oil from a clay vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 祭司从一个陶器里倒出油。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: something hollow that holds what is put inside.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：中空之物，把放进去的东西盛住。

senses.title: A tube in the body
senses.titleCN: 血管、导管：体内的输送管道
senses.definition: a tube or duct in the body that carries blood or another fluid
senses.definitionCN: 体内输送血液或其他液体的管道
senses.example: Cold makes the blood vessels in the fingers narrow.
senses.exampleCN: 寒冷会让手指的血管收缩。
senses.why: The body borrows the container image: the tube holds and moves fluid the way a jug does.
senses.whyCN: 身体借用了容器意象：管道盛住并输送液体，正像一只水罐。

senses.title: A person as a bearer
senses.titleCN: （引申）承载者：作为载体的那个人
senses.definition: a person regarded as a bearer of a quality, a message or a role
senses.definitionCN: 被看作承载某种品质、信息或角色的人
senses.example: In the old story the youngest son is the vessel of the family's hope.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个老故事里，最小的儿子承载着全家的希望。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from thing to person: whoever holds and carries something onward is a vessel for it.
senses.whyCN: 比喻从物移到人：任何盛住并把某物传递下去的人，都是它的容器。

senses.title: A boat in a fixed sense
senses.definition: used in fixed names for types of boat, such as a patrol vessel or a research vessel
senses.definitionCN: 用于巡逻艇、科考船等固定船名说法中
senses.example: A research vessel spent three months mapping the sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一艘科考船花了三个月测绘海底。
senses.why: Here the container idea is frozen into a name for a job at sea.
senses.whyCN: 此时容器观念已经固化成一个命名海上职务的说法。

intro.en: Vessel came from Latin through Old French, and every sense still carries the idea of something hollow that holds.
intro.cn: vessel 经古法语来自拉丁语，每个义项都还带着「中空能盛」的观念。

items.en: Vas meant 'vessel, container, dish'; the plural vasa is still used in anatomy.
items.cn: vas 意为「容器、器皿、盘碟」，其复数 vasa 至今仍在解剖学中使用。

items.en: The diminutive vascellum meant 'a small vessel', and it is the form that reached French.
items.cn: 指小形式 vascellum 意为「小容器」，正是传到法语的那一形式。

items.en: Old French vaisseau meant both a container and a ship, keeping the two ideas together.
items.cn: 古法语 vaisseau 同时指容器与船，把两个观念放在一处。

items.en: English borrowed vessel in the thirteenth century, with ship, container and body-tube senses all present.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 vessel，船、容器与体内管道三个义项当时都已具备。

items.en: Nautical and medical usage split the word: a fishing vessel and a blood vessel barely meet.
items.cn: 航海与医学用法把这个词分开：渔船与血管几乎互不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same container family; the near-meaning group gathers ships and containers with different shades.
note.cn: 形近组收同一容器词族的词；近义组收船只与容器类词，彼此侧重不同。

entries.definition: A decorative container for flowers; the Latin vas survives here too.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「花瓶」，同样来自拉丁语 vas。

entries.definition: The Latin word for vessel, used in anatomical terms such as vas deferens.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语原词，意为容器，用于 vas deferens 等解剖学术语。

entries.definition: A person who owes loyalty to a lord; an unrelated medieval word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「封臣」，来自中古拉丁语，与本词只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A large seagoing vessel; the general word beside the more formal vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「船」，是最通用的说法，vessel 更正式。

entries.definition: A smaller craft; vessel usually implies something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小船」，vessel 通常指更大的船。

entries.definition: Anything that holds something; broader and plainer than vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容器」，比 vessel 更宽泛、更朴素。

entries.definition: A tube in the body or a building; the clinical partner of vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「导管」，是 vessel 在医学语境中的伙伴词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin vas and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语 vas，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: One word, three holders: a vessel carries people, water or blood.
normal.cn: 一个词，三种盛器：vessel 载人、盛水、运血。

normal.en: Latin vas is a container; a ship is a container you sail in.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vas 是容器；船就是你在里面航行的容器。

normal.en: Blood vessel and fishing vessel share the same shape of idea.
normal.cn: 血管与渔船共用同一个形状的观念。

normal.en: Vessel is more formal than ship; officials say vessel.
normal.cn: vessel 比 ship 更正式，官方文件多用 vessel。

normal.en: A vessel must be hollow: the inside matters more than the outside.
normal.cn: 器皿必须是中空的：里面比外面更重要。

abstract.en: Picture a clay jug on a table: the empty space is the useful part, and the clay only holds it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的一只陶罐：真正有用的是中间的空处，陶土只是把它围住。

abstract.en: The word then fills that emptiness with different contents: grain, oil, people, blood.
abstract.cn: 这个词随后用不同的内容填满那片空：谷物、油、人、血。

abstract.en: Anything that carries something safely across a distance can be called a vessel.
abstract.cn: 任何能把某物安全运送过一段距离的东西，都可以称为 vessel。

examples.en: A rescue vessel reached the sinking boat within twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 一艘救援船在二十分钟内赶到了那艘下沉的船旁。

examples.en: Store the oil in a sealed vessel away from heat.
examples.cn: 把油存放在远离热源的密封容器里。

examples.en: The doctor said the vessels around his heart were narrow.
examples.cn: 医生说他心脏周围的血管变窄了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维（ve）塞尔（ssel）」——维塞尔港口的船，一只会装货的大器皿：船；容器

root: 源自拉丁语 vas「容器」的指小形式 vascellum，经古法语 vaisseau「容器、船」进入英语；同源词有 vase、vas。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of vessel all share one hollow shape: a ship carrying people, a jug carrying liquid, a tube carrying blood, and by metaphor a person who carries a hope.
sensesIntro.cn: vessel 的五个义项共用同一个中空形状：船载人、罐盛液、管道运送血液，再经比喻指承载希望的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clay jug on a table, its hollow centre holding what is poured in.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的一只陶罐，中空处盛住倒进去的东西。

branches.en: CONTAINER LINE: the oldest layer, the jug on the table.
branches.cn: 容器线：最古老的一层，桌上的罐子。

branches.en: WATER LINE: the container grows large enough to sail in.
branches.cn: 水面线：容器大到可以航行其中，就成了船。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the same tube shape inside the body.
branches.cn: 体内线：身体内部同样的管状形态。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: a person becomes the vessel of a quality.
branches.cn: 比喻线：人成了某种品质的载体。

branches.en: CONTRAST: ship is plainer, vessel more formal and broader.
branches.cn: 对照线：ship 更朴素，vessel 更正式且范围更广。

intro.en: Vessel is a Latin diminutive that passed through French; the -el ending is a small reminder of its 'little container' origin.
intro.cn: vessel 是经法语而来的拉丁语指小形式；结尾 -el 隐约提示它「小容器」的出身。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vas, with the diminutive vascellum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：vas 及其指小形式 vascellum。

definition_zh: 兽医；老兵；审查；检查
definition_en: an animal doctor, or a person who has served in the armed forces; as a verb, to check someone or something carefully before acceptance
core_image: 给动物看病的人：一件白大褂，面前站着一只不安的小狗
scene: 宠物诊所里，主人轻轻按住小猫的爪子。The vet examined the injured paw carefully before giving the vaccine.
sceneCN: 这里 vet 是「兽医」（第 1 个义项：给动物治病的医生）；句意是兽医在打疫苗前仔细检查受伤的爪子。

pos.zh: 兽医；退伍军人
审查；检查（人或物）是否合格
当兽医；接受审查

collocations.phrase: take the dog to the vet

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 veteranus（老兵）演变而来，本词 vet 是其口语缩略；义为「老兵；经验丰富的人」
veteran 同族形容词，义为「兽医的；动物医疗的」

senses.title: An animal doctor
senses.definition: a person trained to give medical care to sick or injured animals
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、给生病或受伤动物提供医疗照护的人
senses.example: The vet gave the puppy a check-up.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医给小狗做了一次体检。
senses.why: The word is short for veterinary surgeon, the professional who treats animals instead of people.
senses.whyCN: 本词是 veterinary surgeon（兽医外科医生）的口语缩略，指给动物而非人类治病的职业者，核心画面就是白大褂加小动物。

senses.title: A former soldier
senses.definition: a person who has served for a long time or in a war, especially in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 长期服役或经历过战争的人，尤指退伍军人
senses.example: The old vet marched at the head of the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老兵走在游行队伍的最前面。
senses.why: It is the colloquial shortening of veteran, from Latin veteranus meaning one who has grown old in service.
senses.whyCN: 它是 veteran 的口语缩略；拉丁语 veteranus 指「在服役中变老的人」，所以引申为身经百战的老兵。

senses.title: An experienced person in a field
senses.definition: someone with long experience in a particular field or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域或组织中经验丰富的人
senses.example: She is a vet of the film industry, having produced movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她是电影界的老手，制作电影已有三十年。
senses.why: Long service in the army extends metaphorically to long service anywhere, so the old hand and the old soldier share one word.
senses.whyCN: 军中的长期服役被隐喻推广到任何领域的长期资历，于是「老资格的人」与「老兵」共用同一个词。

senses.title: To check carefully before acceptance
senses.definition: to examine someone or something carefully to make sure they are suitable or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细审查某人或某物，确认其合适或安全
senses.example: Every employee is vetted before joining the team.
senses.exampleCN: 每位员工入职前都要经过审查。
senses.why: A doctor examines an animal thoroughly before treating it; that thorough inspection was extended to scrutinizing people and documents.
senses.whyCN: 兽医接诊前要先对动物做彻底检查，这种彻底查验被引申为对人员、文件的严格甄别审查。

senses.title: To treat an animal as a vet
senses.definition: to work as a vet, giving medical treatment to animals
senses.definitionCN: 以兽医身份工作，为动物进行治疗
senses.example: He has vetted farm animals in this village for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这座村子给家畜看病已有二十年。
senses.why: The profession name naturally turns into a verb for doing the profession's work, just like nurse or coach.
senses.whyCN: 职业名词自然转为动词表示从事该职业的工作，正如 nurse（护理）、coach（执教）一样。

intro.en: Vet is a double shortening: veterinary surgeon for the animal doctor, and veteran for the old soldier.
intro.cn: vet 是双重缩略：作为「兽医」是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略；作为「老兵」是 veteran 的缩略。

items.en: veteranus meant 'aged, one who has served long', from vetus, 'old'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veteranus 意为「年长的、长期服役的」，词根 vetus 意为「老」。

items.en: veterinarius described things relating to beasts of burden, the root of veterinary.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veterinarius 描述与驮兽相关的事物，是 veterinary 的来源。

items.en: Veteran entered English for old soldiers; veterinary surgeon named the animal doctor.
items.cn: veteran 于十七至十九世纪进入英语，指老兵；veterinary surgeon 指动物医生。

items.en: Both long titles were clipped to vet in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，两个冗长的头衔都被缩短成 vet。

items.en: The noun vet was turned into a verb meaning to scrutinize before acceptance.
items.cn: 名词 vet 又转为动词，表示「录用前的审查甄别」。

note.en: Watch the clipped forms: vet comes from two long words, and neighbors like veto only look alike.
note.cn: 注意缩略形式：vet 来自两个长词，而 veto（否决）等邻居只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: an official power to reject a decision or proposal
entries.definitionCN: 否决权；否决。只是拼写相近，词源不同（拉丁语 vetare，禁止）。

entries.definition: a person with long experience, especially a former soldier
entries.definitionCN: 老兵；经验丰富者。vet 作「老兵」解时正是它的口语缩略。

entries.definition: relating to the medical care of animals
entries.definitionCN: 兽医的；动物医疗的。vet 作「兽医」解时源自其首音节。

entries.definition: a doctor who treats human patients
entries.definitionCN: 医生；内科医生。对象是人类，与兽医保卫的对象相对。

entries.definition: a person who tests or inspects others formally
entries.definitionCN: 审查者；检查者。与 vet 动词义的「甄别审查」相近，但更正式。

entries.definition: to examine something very carefully
entries.definitionCN: 仔细审查。与 vet 的动词义几乎重合，但不含「录用前把关」的语感。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built from the word's real history and uses.
normalIntro.cn: 基于词源与真实用法的五条联想。

normal.en: Vet clips veterinary surgeon: the vet vets your pet.
normal.cn: vet 是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略：兽医给宠物看病（vet your pet）。

normal.en: Vet also clips veteran: the war vet sits beside the dog vet.
normal.cn: vet 也是 veteran 的缩略：老兵与兽医共用一个短词。

normal.en: To vet a candidate is to give him a full check-up, like an animal at the clinic.
normal.cn: 审查候选人类似兽医接诊：先做全面「体检」再放行。

normal.en: Latin vetus means old; veterans are those grown old in service.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 vetus 意为「老」，老兵就是服役到老的人。

normal.en: Verb forms double the T: vet, vetted, vetting.
normal.cn: 动词变化双写 T：vet, vetted, vetting。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with one pocket for pills and another for medals.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂，一个口袋装药片，另一个装勋章。

abstract.en: Imagine a small dog waiting quietly under the clinic lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象诊灯下安静等待的小狗。

abstract.en: Feel a gatekeeper's stamp: checked, approved, allowed through.
abstract.cn: 感受把关者的印章：查毕、合格、放行。

examples.en: We took the sick cat to the vet this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我们带生病的猫去看兽医。

examples.en: His grandfather was a navy vet who loved telling stories.
examples.cn: 他的祖父是位海军老兵，爱讲故事。

examples.en: All news reports are vetted before publication.
examples.cn: 所有新闻报道发表前都要经过审查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂它」——兽医的工作就是喂它、护理它；老兵回营也是为了有口饭「喂它」。

root: vet 作名词有两条来源：一是 veterinary（拉丁语 veterinarius「与驮兽有关的」）的缩略，指兽医；二是 veteran（拉丁语 veteranus，词根 vetus「老」）的缩略，指老兵。动词义由「彻底检查」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the animal doctor and the old soldier, the word stretches to experienced hands and then to the act of scrutiny.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「兽医」「老兵」两个名词核心，延伸出「老手」的比喻义，再引申出动词「审查」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short white coat that serves animals, soldiers, and the checkpoint
core.cn: 核心意象：一件服务动物、军人，并守在检查关卡前的白大褂

branches.en: The clinic work
branches.cn: 诊所里的诊疗工作，从名词职业到动词行医。

branches.en: The battle-tested soldier
branches.cn: 身经百战的退伍军人。

branches.en: The veteran of any trade
branches.cn: 任何行业的资深老手。

branches.en: The thorough check before trust
branches.cn: 信任之前的彻底核查。

branches.en: From inspection to clearance
branches.cn: 从检查到放行，把关的完整闭环。

intro.en: The family of vet- rests on Latin vetus, old, and branches into medicine, war, and checking.
intro.cn: vet- 词族建立在拉丁语 vetus（老）之上，分支延伸到医疗、战争与审查领域。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives that share the root of growing old in service.
latinIntro.cn: 共享「服役至老」这一词根的拉丁同源词。

items.example: veterani were settled on farmland after service
items.exampleCN: 退伍老兵战后被安置到农田。

derivatives.zh: vet 的全形来源之一，义为「老兵；老手」
vet 的全形来源之一，义为「兽医的」

definition_zh: 经由；经过（某地）；通过、借助（某人或某手段）
definition_en: by way of a place, or by means of a person or method
core_image: 一条路线在纸上转弯，绕过一座山，最后才到达目的地
scene: 邮件在三个城市之间转了一圈，最后才落到桌上。We flew to Rome via Zurich.
sceneCN: 这里 via 是「经由某地」（第 1 个义项：路线经过某地）；句意为我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。那条绕过山再到的路线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 介词：经由、经过；通过、借助

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「高架桥」，与 via 同源于拉丁语 via「道路」
动词，义为「偏离」，同源于拉丁语 via
形容词，义为「明显的」，字面义为「在路上迎面遇上」，同根
形容词，义为「琐碎的」，字面义为「三岔路口的」，同根

senses.title: By way of a place
senses.titleCN: 经由某地：路线经过而不停留
senses.definition: travelling through a place on the way to another
senses.definitionCN: 在前往另一地途中经过某地
senses.example: We flew to Rome via Zurich.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。
senses.why: Latin via is a road; the preposition simply names the road taken without claiming a stop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 via 就是道路；这个介词只说走的是哪条路，并不表示停下来。

senses.title: By means of
senses.titleCN: 通过、借助：靠某种手段完成
senses.definition: by means of a particular method, person or service
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种方法、人或服务实现
senses.example: We sent the documents via email to save time.
senses.exampleCN: 为了省时间，我们通过电子邮件发了文件。
senses.why: The road becomes a figure of speech: the channel that carries the action.
senses.whyCN: 道路变成了比喻：承载这个动作的通道。

senses.title: Through an intermediary
senses.titleCN: 经某人转手：不直接对接
senses.definition: through a person or office acting in between
senses.definitionCN: 通过居间的人或机构
senses.example: The message reached him via his assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 消息通过他的助理传到了他那里。
senses.why: The route now runs through a person rather than through a town.
senses.whyCN: 路线这次穿过的是一个人，而不是一座城镇。

senses.title: Through a route or medium
senses.titleCN: 通过某一路径或媒介：抽象通道
senses.definition: through a particular route, path or medium
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定路径或媒介
senses.example: Data travels via underground cables to the other building.
senses.exampleCN: 数据经地下电缆传到另一栋楼。
senses.why: A cable is a road for electricity, and the word applies without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 电缆是电的道路，这个词不再变形就直接用上了。

intro.en: Via is the Latin noun for road, taken whole into English and pressed into service as a preposition.
intro.cn: via 是拉丁语里表示「道路」的名词，整块进入英语后被用作介词。

items.en: The noun via meant a road, way or street, and also a method.
items.cn: 名词 via 意为道路、路径，也可指方法。

items.en: In phrases such as via Appia the ablative already worked as by way of, a road name in use.
items.cn: 在 via Appia 这类短语里，这个夺格形式已经带有「经……路」的意味。

items.en: English borrowed via in the eighteenth century as a preposition of route.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 via，用作表路线的介词。

items.en: Rail, aviation and postal writing spread it through travel timetables.
items.cn: 铁路、航空与邮政文书把它普及到旅行时刻表里。

items.en: Modern usage adds the abstract sense, so documents now travel via email.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了抽象含义，于是文件可以通过邮件旅行。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin road root; the near-meaning group holds prepositions of route and means.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁「道路」词根；近义组收表示路线与手段的介词。

entries.definition: A road carried over a valley; literally a road leader.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高架桥」，字面即「引路之桥」。

entries.definition: To leave the road; hence to stray.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「偏离」，字面即离开道路。

entries.definition: Literally lying in the road, hence plain to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」，字面即「在路中遇到」。

entries.definition: Of a crossroads, hence common and slight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「琐碎的」，由「三岔路口」引申为常见而轻微。

entries.definition: By way of, inside and out the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，从一头进、另一头出。

entries.definition: By means of, or past a point on a route.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「靠、经」，也可指路过某点。

entries.definition: In every part, stronger than via.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「遍及」，比 via 更强。

entries.definition: Following the length of a road or river.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「沿着」，顺着路或河的长度走。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal road and the modern habits of travel and mail.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面上的「道路」，以及现代出行与邮件的习惯。

normal.en: Via is Latin for road, and roads explain the word.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语的「道路」，道路解释了它。

normal.en: Fly via Paris means Paris is on the way, not the destination.
normal.cn: fly via Paris 指巴黎在途中，不是目的地。

normal.en: Send it via email means the message takes a digital road.
normal.cn: send it via email 指消息走了一条数字的路。

normal.en: Obvious, deviate and trivial all come from the same road word.
normal.cn: obvious、deviate、trivial 都出自同一个「道路」词。

normal.en: Via does not mean in: you do not stop there for long.
normal.cn: via 不等于 in：你不在那里久留。

abstract.en: Via names the path rather than the place: it tells you how the thing got here.
abstract.cn: via 命名的是路径而非地点：它告诉你东西是怎么过来的。

abstract.en: Anything that moves needs a road, so the word stretches to cables, satellites and people.
abstract.cn: 凡会动的东西都需要一条路，于是这个词扩展到电缆、卫星和人。

abstract.en: To name the route is already to hint at the motive, which is why the same word covers means.
abstract.cn: 说出路线已经在暗示成因，所以同一个词也能表示手段。

examples.en: We returned home via the coast road.
examples.cn: 我们沿着海边公路回家。

examples.en: Please send your application via the website.
examples.cn: 请通过网站提交申请。

examples.en: He learned the news via a friend in the office.
examples.cn: 他从办公室的一位朋友那里得到这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外啊」——外啊，外面这条路经过咱们这儿：经由

root: 直接来自拉丁语名词 via「道路、方法」，十八世纪起在英语中作介词使用；同根词有 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial。

sensesIntro.en: Via travels from a real road, to a method, to a person in between, to an abstract channel.
sensesIntro.cn: via 从真实的道路出发，走到方法、居间的人，再到抽象的通道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a map that bends around a hill before reaching the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条线绕过小山，才到目的地。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: a place passed on the way.
branches.cn: 路线线：途中经过的地点。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: the means by which it is done.
branches.cn: 方法线：办成事所借助的手段。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: a message relayed by someone else.
branches.cn: 人际线：由别人转达的消息。

branches.en: CABLE LINE: an abstract path or medium.
branches.cn: 线路线：抽象的路径或媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: via names the way, in names the place.
branches.cn: 对照线：via 说路，in 说地。

intro.en: Via has no affixes, but the Latin noun it comes from hides inside several English words.
intro.cn: via 没有词缀，但构成它的拉丁名词藏在好几个英语词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun via, road, survives in viaduct, deviate, obvious and trivial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 via「道路」残留在 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial 里。

items.example: It forms deviate, to leave the road.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deviate，即离开道路。

items.example: It forms obvious, in the way.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 obvious，即在路中遇到。

items.example: It forms trivial, of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trivial，即三岔路口的。

definition_zh: 能存活的；可行的；可实施的；能维持的；有生存力的
definition_en: able to stay alive, or able to work and continue successfully in practice
core_image: 一株幼苗顶开土面站稳，旁边一只空壳种子倒在土里，记录牌上画着发芽曲线
scene: 温室里，一株幼苗顶开土面，叶片慢慢展开，旁边另一粒种子却始终没有动静。Only two of the seeds were viable after the long drought.
sceneCN: 这里指种子具有存活发芽的能力（第 1 个义项：能存活、能生长）；句意为漫长干旱之后只有两粒种子还能存活。图中可辨识物件：幼苗、未发芽的种子、育苗盘、记录牌。

pos.zh: 能存活的；可行的；可维持的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加表示能力的名词词尾构成，义为「存活能力；可行性」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以可行的方式」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不能存活的；不可行的」

senses.title: Able to stay alive
senses.definition: of a living thing, seed or cell, able to live and grow under present conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指生物、种子或细胞在现有条件下能够存活并生长
senses.example: Only two of the seeds were viable after the long drought.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长干旱之后，只有两粒种子还能存活。
senses.why: The French source joins a word for life to a suffix of ability, so the first sense is simply able to live.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源把一个表示「生命」的词接上表能力的词尾，因此第一义就是「能活」。

senses.title: Able to be carried out
senses.definition: of a plan or method, practical enough to be put into effect
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或方法足够实际，可以付诸实施
senses.example: The engineers proposed a viable route around the flooded valley.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提出了一条绕开被淹山谷的可行路线。
senses.why: The word moved from organisms to plans: what can survive contact with reality is viable.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从生物转到计划：经得起现实接触的，就是可行的。

senses.title: Able to survive financially
senses.definition: of a business or project, able to cover its costs and keep operating
senses.definitionCN: 指企业或项目能覆盖成本并持续运转
senses.example: The farm became viable only after it switched to direct sales.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场直到改做直销才变得能维持下去。
senses.why: Money is the environment in which a business lives or dies, so the metaphor stays biological.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是企业生死存亡的环境，因此这个比喻仍是生物学的。

senses.title: Able to keep an organisation alive
senses.definition: of an institution or industry, strong enough to continue rather than collapse
senses.definitionCN: 指机构或行业足够强健，能继续存在而不崩溃
senses.example: Analysts asked whether the small airline was still viable.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士追问这家小航空公司是否仍有生存力。
senses.why: Here viability is about the whole body, not a single plan or budget line.
senses.whyCN: 这里的生存力关乎整个机体，而非单一计划或一条预算。

senses.title: Able to continue as a tradition
senses.definition: of a custom, language or system, likely to survive into the future
senses.definitionCN: 指习俗、语言或制度有可能延续到未来
senses.example: Few believed the village school was still viable with so few children.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有人相信，孩子这么少，村校还能办得下去。
senses.why: The metaphor extends to anything that must renew itself to last.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻扩展到任何必须自我更新才能延续的事物。

senses.title: A practical substitute
senses.titleCN: 可实际采用的替代方案
senses.definition: of an alternative, realistic enough to replace what is currently used
senses.definitionCN: 指替代方案足够现实，可以取代当前所用之物
senses.example: Solar power is now a viable alternative to diesel in remote areas.
senses.exampleCN: 在偏远地区，太阳能如今是柴油的可行替代方案。
senses.why: A substitute must survive comparison, which is why the word so often sits before alternative.
senses.whyCN: 替代品必须经得起比较，所以这个词常放在「替代方案」前面。

senses.title: Able to reproduce and persist
senses.definition: of a population, large enough and healthy enough to breed and persist
senses.definitionCN: 指种群规模与健康程度足以繁殖并持续存在
senses.example: Conservationists set a target for a viable population of the species.
senses.exampleCN: 保护工作者为该物种设定了可存续种群的目标。
senses.why: Ecology makes viability a property of a group, not of one organism.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把「可存活」变成群体的属性，而非单个生物的属性。

senses.title: Acceptable in political or legal terms
senses.definition: of a proposal, able to win acceptance without being rejected outright
senses.definitionCN: 指提案能被接受，而不会被直接否决
senses.example: The reform was technically sound but not politically viable.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革在技术上站得住，但在政治上行不通。
senses.why: A proposal also lives in an environment: it must survive the room it is presented to.
senses.whyCN: 提案也生活在环境里：它必须熬过被提交的那个房间。

senses.title: A candidate with a real chance
senses.definition: of a person in a contest, having a realistic chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 指竞争中有现实成功机会的人
senses.example: Party leaders looked for a viable candidate in the northern district.
senses.exampleCN: 党内领导层在北部选区寻找有胜算的候选人。
senses.why: A candidacy is another life that must survive the contest to continue.
senses.whyCN: 候选资格是另一种必须熬过竞争才能延续的生命。

intro.en: Viable joins a Latin word for life to a suffix meaning able to: the original sense is simply able to live, and English extended it to plans that can survive.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语表示「生命」的词接上表「能够」的词尾：本义就是「能活」，英语再扩展到「能经得起现实」的计划。

items.en: vita meant life, and it is the stem behind vital and vitality as well.
items.cn: vita 意为「生命」，也是 vital 与 vitality 的词干。

items.en: French shortened the Latin stem into vie, the everyday word for life.
items.cn: 法语把拉丁词干缩成 vie，即日常用语中的「生命」。

items.en: French built viable from vie plus a suffix of ability, first for a fetus able to live outside the womb.
items.cn: 法语用 vie 加表能力的词尾构成 viable，最初指胎儿能离开子宫存活。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the nineteenth century, first in the medical sense; the exact first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个形容词，最初用于医学含义；具体首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it from organisms to projects, firms and proposals that can survive reality.
items.cn: 二十世纪把它从生物扩展到能在现实中存续的项目、企业与提案。

items.en: Policy and ecology now speak of viable alternatives and viable populations.
items.cn: 政策与生态学现在会说「可行的替代方案」与「可存续的种群」。

note.en: The first group shares the life root or looks close; the second group names nearby ideas of practicality, and the note separates viable from feasible.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生命」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的实用性说法，说明中把 viable 与 feasible 分开。

entries.definition: The noun for the ability to live or to succeed in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指存活或实践中成功的能力。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a way that can be sustained.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指以可持续的方式做某事。

entries.definition: Not able to live or to work in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能存活或在实践中行不通。

entries.definition: Necessary to life or to success; it shares the life stem but stresses necessity.
entries.definitionCN: 指对生命或成功必不可少；共享「生命」词干，但强调必要。

entries.definition: Likely to change; it looks close but comes from a root meaning to vary, not to live.
entries.definitionCN: 指易变的；形近，但词根意为「变化」，而非「生命」。

entries.definition: Possible to do with the means available; it asks whether a thing can be done, not whether it can live on.
entries.definitionCN: 指用现有手段可以做到；它问的是「能不能做」，而非「能不能活下去」。

entries.definition: Practical enough to operate; plainer and often about a method or arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指足够实用、能运转；更朴素，常指方法或安排。

entries.definition: Able to continue over time without exhausting its base; it stresses endurance, not first survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指能长期持续而不耗尽基础；强调持久，而非初次存活。

entries.definition: Alive now; for a fetus or organism it is the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 指当下活着的；用于胎儿或生物时是最朴素的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real life stem, the real medical origin and the real contrast with feasible.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「生命」词干、真实的医学起源，以及与 feasible 的真实区别。

normal.en: Vita is life and -able is able: viable is literally able to live, and a plan must also live.
normal.cn: vita 是生命，-able 是能够：viable 字面上就是「能活」，而计划也得活下去。

normal.en: A seed that sprouts and a business that pays its bills share one adjective.
normal.cn: 发芽的种子与付得起账的企业共享同一个形容词。

normal.en: Viable alternative, commercially viable and viable population are three real phrases.
normal.cn: 可行的替代方案、商业上可行与可存续种群是三个真实搭配。

normal.en: Feasible asks can it be done; viable asks can it stay alive after it is done.
normal.cn: feasible 问「做得成吗」；viable 问「做成之后活得下去吗」。

normal.en: The noun is viability, the negative is nonviable, and both keep the life image.
normal.cn: 名词是 viability，否定形式是 nonviable，两者都保留「生命」意象。

abstract.en: Viability is survival under present conditions, which means the conditions can always take it away.
abstract.cn: 可行性是在现有条件下存活，这意味着条件随时可以把它收回。

abstract.en: A plan is an organism in the environment of budgets, habits and politics.
abstract.cn: 计划是一个生活在预算、习惯与政治环境中的生物。

abstract.en: What is viable is not necessarily good; some harmful things survive very well.
abstract.cn: 能存活的不一定是好的；有些有害之物活得非常好。

examples.en: The clinic kept the premature infant in an incubator until it was viable.
examples.cn: 诊所把早产儿放在保温箱里，直到他能存活。

examples.en: Recycling becomes economically viable once collection is combined with other services.
examples.cn: 一旦把收集与其他服务合并，回收在经济上就变得可行。

examples.en: The party needed a viable candidate before it could contest the seat.
examples.cn: 该党需要一名有胜算的候选人，才能争夺这个席位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「外尔伯」——「能活」；能活下来，才算可行

root: 来自法语 viable「能活的」← vie「生命」+ -able「能够」，vie 出自拉丁语 vita「生命」。英语十九世纪借入，先用于胎儿存活的医学含义。来源链清楚，首见年份为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a living seed through plans, finances, institutions, traditions, substitutes, populations, politics and candidates.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从能活的种子，经过计划、财务、机构、传统、替代方案、种群、政治与候选人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seedling stands up out of the soil while the seed beside it stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株幼苗从土里立起来，旁边那粒种子却始终没有打开。

branches.en: THE ORGANISM: a seed, a fetus or a whole population that can keep living.
branches.cn: 生物：能继续存活的种子、胎儿或整个种群。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND THE SUBSTITUTE: a route or alternative that survives reality.
branches.cn: 计划与替代：经得起现实的路线或替代方案。

branches.en: THE MONEY AND THE INSTITUTION: a firm or industry that can cover its costs.
branches.cn: 钱与机构：能覆盖成本的企业或行业。

branches.en: THE TRADITION: a school, language or custom able to renew itself.
branches.cn: 传统：能自我更新的学校、语言或习俗。

branches.en: THE ROOM AND THE RACE: a proposal or candidate that can survive a vote.
branches.cn: 房间与竞赛：能熬过投票的提案或候选人。

intro.en: Viable is a life stem plus an ability suffix, borrowed whole from French.
intro.cn: 这个词是「生命」词干加表能力的词尾，整体借自法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies vita and vitalis; French supplies vie and viable, and English took the French adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 vita 与 vitalis；法语提供了 vie 与 viable，英语借入的是法语形容词。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名生命本身。

items.example: The French form carries the stem forward.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式把词干传下去。

items.example: The borrowed word begins as a medical term.
items.exampleCN: 借入的词最初是医学术语。

items.meaning: the ability to live or work
items.example: The noun adds a quality ending.
A sister adjective keeps the life stem.
items.exampleCN: 同族形容词保留「生命」词干。

items.example: It forms nonviable, the failed case.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 nonviable，即失败的情形。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加能力名词词尾构成，义为「可行性」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以可行方式」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「不能存活的」

definition_zh: 振动；震颤；（声音）回荡；颤动
definition_en: to move quickly and slightly to and fro, or to sound with a shaking tone
core_image: 手机静音放在桌面，屏幕亮起前桌子轻轻嗡了一下
scene: 车到站时，地板先轻微一颤，行李箱的拉杆跟着抖。The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
sceneCN: 这里 vibrate 是「振动」（第 1 个义项：快速而轻微地来回运动）；句意为列车进站时地板在振动。桌上手机嗡一下的那种轻颤就是这个动作的意思。

pos.zh: 振动；颤动；回荡

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ion 构成，义为「振动；颤动」
现在分词作形容词，义为「震动的；颤动的」
加后缀 -atory 构成，义为「振动的」

senses.title: To shake quickly and slightly
senses.definition: to move back and forth very fast and with a small range
senses.definitionCN: 以很小的幅度快速来回运动
senses.example: The floor vibrated as the train pulled into the station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车进站时地板在震动。
senses.why: Latin vibrare described a swift, small shake, and that is still the core motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vibrare 指的正是快速而小幅的抖动，这仍是核心动作。

senses.title: To sound with a shaking tone
senses.definition: to produce or carry a sound that keeps shaking in the air
senses.definitionCN: 发出或在空气中持续震荡的声音
senses.example: His voice vibrated with anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他的声音因愤怒而发颤。
senses.why: A struck string shakes the air, and the shaking is what we hear as a living tone.
senses.whyCN: 被拨动的弦使空气震动，我们听到的那种「活」的音色就是这种震动。

senses.title: To be full of a strong feeling
senses.definition: to seem to shake with excitement, energy, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 因兴奋、活力或情绪而显得震动
senses.example: The hall vibrated with applause.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里掌声雷动。
senses.why: When a crowded room shakes with sound, the place itself seems to tremble.
senses.whyCN: 满场的声音让整个空间都在震，地方本身也仿佛在颤。

senses.title: Of a machine, to work with a hum
senses.definition: to run with a steady small shaking, as an engine does
senses.definitionCN: 如发动机那样带着持续的小幅震动运转
senses.example: The old fridge vibrates all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧冰箱整夜嗡嗡作响。
senses.why: Machines turned the natural shake of matter into a daily background noise.
senses.whyCN: 机器把物质固有的抖动变成了日常的背景噪音。

senses.title: To swing between two choices
senses.definition: to move quickly between two states, as a mind between choices
senses.definitionCN: 像心思在两种选择间快速来回
senses.example: He vibrated between hope and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 他在希望与恐惧之间摇摆。
senses.why: A movement to and fro can describe a mind as easily as a string.
senses.whyCN: 来回摆动既可以形容琴弦，也可以形容心思。

intro.en: Vibrate comes from Latin vibrare, to shake or brandish, a motion small and fast.
intro.cn: vibrate 来自拉丁语 vibrare（抖动、挥舞），指的是一种小而快的运动。

items.en: Vibrare meant to shake, to quiver, and also to wave a weapon.
items.cn: vibrare 意为抖动、颤动，也表示挥舞武器。

items.en: The noun vibratio described a quivering movement.
items.cn: 名词 vibratio 描述颤动的运动。

items.en: English took vibrate in the seventeenth century, first for shaking bodies.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入 vibrate，最初用于物体的抖动。

items.en: Sound and engines gave the word its everyday modern senses.
items.cn: 声音与发动机赋予它现代日常的含义。

items.en: Phones added the sense of a silent buzz in the pocket.
items.cn: 手机又添上口袋里无声的一阵嗡动。

note.en: The first group holds the vibration family, the second the nearby verbs of shaking and steadying.
note.cn: 第一组是 vibration 词族，第二组是表示晃动与稳定的相近动词。

entries.definition: a shaking movement
entries.definitionCN: 振动

entries.definition: of or causing vibration
entries.definitionCN: 振动的

entries.definition: full of energy and colour
entries.definitionCN: 充满活力的

entries.definition: a shaking in a sung note
entries.definitionCN: 颤音

entries.definition: to move with larger, rougher force
entries.definitionCN: 摇动

entries.definition: to shake from fear or cold
entries.definitionCN: 发抖

entries.definition: to shake in a light, quick way
entries.definitionCN: 轻微颤动

entries.definition: to make firm and still
entries.definitionCN: 使稳定

normalIntro.en: A slip of -ate on the Latin stem vibr- gives a verb for any fast, small shake.
normalIntro.cn: 在拉丁词干 vibr- 上加 -ate，就得到表示任何快速小抖动的动词。

normal.en: Vibrate, vibration, vibrant all share the Latin stem vibr-.
normal.cn: vibrate、vibration、vibrant 共有拉丁词干 vibr-。

normal.en: A string, a floor, a phone: the smaller the shake, the better the word.
normal.cn: 琴弦、地板、手机：抖得越小，越适合这个词。

normal.en: British stress falls on the second syllable, American often on the first.
normal.cn: 英式重音在第二音节，美式常在第一音节。

normal.en: Keep the final -e before -ion: vibration.
normal.cn: 加 -ion 前保留词尾 -e：vibration。

normal.en: Old Latin vibrare also meant to brandish a spear.
normal.cn: 古拉丁语 vibrare 还表示挥舞长矛。

abstract.en: Feel a phoned handset humming on a wooden table.
abstract.cn: 感受桌上的手机在震。

abstract.en: See a violin string after the bow has left it.
abstract.cn: 想琴弓离开后仍在颤的琴弦。

abstract.en: Hear a whole hall shaking with clapping.
abstract.cn: 听整个大厅被掌声震得发响。

examples.en: The windows vibrated whenever a truck went past.
examples.cn: 每当有卡车经过，窗户就震动。

examples.en: Her voice vibrated with excitement on the phone.
examples.cn: 电话里她的声音因兴奋而发颤。

examples.en: Set the phone to vibrate during the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会时把手机调成振动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪不瑞特」——歪着的架子不稳，一碰就抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 vibrare（抖动；挥舞）→ vibratio（颤动）→ 英语 vibrate

sensesIntro.en: One verb of tiny fast motion grows into sound, into a crowded hall, into engines, and finally into a wavering mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示极快小幅运动的动词，长成声音、长成满场掌声、长成机器嗡鸣，最后长成摇摆不定的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone buzzing on a wooden table.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桌上嗡动的手机。

branches.en: The motion branch: a floor shaking as the train arrives.
branches.cn: 运动分支：列车进站时震动的车厢地板。

branches.en: The sound branch: a voice shaking with anger.
branches.cn: 声音分支：因愤怒而颤抖的声音。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a hall trembling with applause.
branches.cn: 人群分支：被掌声震动的大厅。

branches.en: The machine branch: the fridge humming all night.
branches.cn: 机器分支：整夜嗡鸣的冰箱。

branches.en: The mind branch: swinging between hope and fear.
branches.cn: 心思分支：在希望与恐惧间摇摆。

intro.en: The Latin stem vibr- means to shake; -ate, -ion, and -ant build verb and nouns from it.
intro.cn: 拉丁词干 vibr- 意为抖动，-ate、-ion、-ant 由它构成动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vibrare yielded English vibrate, vibration, and vibrant, all keeping the small quick shake.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vibrare 派生英语 vibrate、vibration、vibrant，都保留了小而快的抖动。

items.example: Vibrate is the act of shaking.
Vibrant means alive with quick energy.
items.exampleCN: vibrant 意为充满轻快活力的。

items.meaning: to shake from fear or cold
items.example: He trembled, but the bridge vibrated.
The arrow quivered in the target.
Steady the camera before the shot.

items.meaning: a tremble in a sung note
items.example: The singer added vibrato to the long note.
items.exampleCN: 歌手在长音上加了颤音。

latinEntries.meaning: to shake, to quiver, to brandish

definition_zh: 受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者；（事故、疾病的）受害者
definition_en: a person harmed, injured or killed as the result of a crime, accident or other event
core_image: 一队被牵去献祭的牲畜，脖子上系着彩带，走在前头
scene: 火灾过后，邻居们围在被烧黑的门口，不知道该说什么。The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
sceneCN: 这里 victim 是「受害者」（第 1 个义项：在灾难或罪案中受到伤害的人）；句意为洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。被牵去献祭的牲畜，就是这个词最早的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者

collocations.zh: 装可怜、摆出受害者姿态

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词加 -ize 构成
名词，义为「受害、迫害」
形容词，义为「无受害者的」，如 victimless crime
名词，义为「受害者身份」

senses.title: One harmed by another
senses.titleCN: 受害者：被罪案或他人伤害的人
senses.definition: a person harmed by a crime or by someone else’s action
senses.definitionCN: 被犯罪或他人行为伤害的人
senses.example: The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。
senses.why: Latin victima was the animal led to sacrifice; the modern sense keeps the picture of someone taken and harmed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victima 是被牵去献祭的牲畜；现代含义仍保留「被夺去并受伤害」的画面。

senses.title: One killed or injured
senses.titleCN: 遇难者：在事故或灾害中伤亡的人
senses.definition: a person killed or injured in an accident or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或灾害中死亡或受伤的人
senses.example: Road victims have fallen since the speed limit changed.
senses.exampleCN: 限速改变后，道路事故的死伤者减少了。
senses.why: No agent is needed here; the harm comes from events, not from a criminal.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要施害者：伤害来自事件，而不是罪犯。

senses.title: One suffering from illness
senses.definition: a person suffering from a disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 受某种疾病或状况折磨的人
senses.example: Many victims of the disease do not know they have it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多患这种病的人并不知道自己有。
senses.why: Illness is treated as an outer force that takes prisoners, much like an accident.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被当成一种抓走人的外部力量，与事故相似。

senses.title: A sacrifice
senses.titleCN: 牺牲品：为了别的目的而被舍弃的人或物
senses.definition: someone or something given up for another purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为别的目的被舍弃的人或物
senses.example: The old building became a victim of the redevelopment plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老建筑成了重建计划的牺牲品。
senses.why: Buildings cannot feel pain, yet the pattern holds: something old is given up for something new.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不会感到疼痛，但模式仍在：旧的东西为新的东西被舍弃了。

senses.title: A self-chosen role
senses.titleCN: 装出的受害者：把自己当成被亏待的人
senses.definition: a role taken on by someone who claims unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 某人自称受到不公而摆出的姿态
senses.example: He always plays the victim when the plan goes wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一出错，他就摆出受害者的姿态。
senses.why: The word turns ironic here: the person chooses the role instead of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词带了反讽：角色是自己选的，而不是被强加的。

intro.en: Victim comes from Latin victima, a beast offered in sacrifice, and has kept the sense of being taken and harmed.
intro.cn: victim 来自拉丁语 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，一直保留着「被夺去并受伤害」的意思。

items.en: Victima named the animal led to the altar, chosen and given up.
items.cn: victima 指被牵上祭坛的牲畜，被选中并被舍弃。

items.en: The word belonged to the language of sacrifice, with its sense of a life taken.
items.cn: 这个词属于献祭的语言，含「夺走一条生命」的意思。

items.en: French kept victime for a creature sacrificed or killed, sacred or not.
items.cn: 法语保留 victime，指被献祭或被杀的生命，不论是否神圣。

items.en: English took victim in the fifteenth century, widening it to anyone who suffers harm.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 victim，扩展到任何受到伤害的人。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to crime, disaster, disease and, ironically, to a chosen pose.
items.cn: 现代用法把它用于罪案、灾害、疾病，甚至反讽地指一种自愿摆出的姿态。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the victim- family; the near-meaning group holds words for those who suffer or are lost.
note.cn: 形近组沿 victim- 家族；近义组收表示受难者与损失的词。

entries.definition: To make someone a victim, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: The act of treating someone as a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害、被迫害」。

entries.definition: Having no harmed party, as in some crimes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无受害者的」。

entries.definition: The state of being a victim.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受害者身份」。

entries.definition: One who endures pain or illness, often long term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受苦者、患者」，多为长期。

entries.definition: One killed or wounded in fighting or an accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡者」，多用于战争与事故。

entries.definition: One who lived through the same event, the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幸存者」，同一事件的另一面。

entries.definition: The one aimed at, before any harm is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，伤害尚未发生前的一方。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the sacrifice picture and the phrase fall victim to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「献祭」的画面与 fall victim to 这一搭配。

normal.en: Victim once meant the animal led to the altar.
normal.cn: victim 原本指被牵上祭坛的牲畜。

normal.en: Fall victim to a scam means the trick caught you.
normal.cn: fall victim to a scam 指你被这个骗局抓住了。

normal.en: Victims of a flood are harmed by weather, not by a criminal.
normal.cn: 洪水的受害者是被天气所害，而不是被罪犯。

normal.en: Victimize is the verb: to make someone a victim.
normal.cn: victimize 是动词：使某人成为受害者。

normal.en: Playing the victim is a choice of role, not a fact.
normal.cn: playing the victim 是一种角色选择，不是事实。

abstract.en: The word began in sacrifice, and every later use keeps the shape of a life given up for something else.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于献祭，此后每种用法都保留着「为别的东西交出生命」的形状。

abstract.en: A victim is defined by what happened to them, which is why the word is passive in grammar and in feeling.
abstract.cn: 受害者是由遭遇定义的，所以这个词在语法和情感上都是被动的。

abstract.en: Naming someone a victim gives them sympathy but takes away agency, a tension the word never resolves.
abstract.cn: 称某人为受害者，给了他同情却拿走了主动性，这个矛盾这个词从未解决。

examples.en: The charity helps victims of domestic violence.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构帮助家庭暴力的受害者。

examples.en: Many small shops fell victim to the rise in rents.
examples.cn: 许多小店成了租金上涨的牺牲品。

examples.en: She was the victim of a cruel joke.
examples.cn: 她是一个恶作剧的受害者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克提姆」——维克（围）克（制）提（他）姆（母亲）受害了：受害者

root: 源自拉丁语名词 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，经法语 victime 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 victimize、victimization、victimhood。

sensesIntro.en: Victim stretches from the sacrificed animal to crime, accidents, illness, lost buildings and a chosen pose.
sensesIntro.cn: victim 从被献祭的牲畜，延伸到罪案、事故、疾病、被拆的建筑与自愿摆出的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal led to the altar with ribbons on its neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头脖子系着彩带、被牵向祭坛的牲畜。

branches.en: CRIME LINE: harmed by another person.
branches.cn: 罪案线：被他人所害。

branches.en: DISASTER LINE: injured by events.
branches.cn: 灾害线：被事件所伤。

branches.en: ILLNESS LINE: struck by disease.
branches.cn: 疾病线：被病痛击中。

branches.en: FIGURE LINE: a building given up, a role worn on purpose.
branches.cn: 比喻线：被舍弃的建筑，故意披上的角色。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a victim receives harm, a target is only aimed at.
branches.cn: 对照线：受害者已受到伤害，目标只是被瞄准。

intro.en: Victim is a complete Latin noun; English relatives add -ize, -ization, -hood and -less.
intro.cn: victim 是完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词加 -ize、-ization、-hood、-less。

latinIntro.en: The single Latin form is victima, a ritual word without a clear further root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式只有一个 victima，是礼仪用语，更早的词根并不明确。

definition_zh: 景色；看法；视野；观看
definition_en: what can be seen from a place, or the way a person thinks about something
core_image: 推开旅馆的窗，整片湖面铺在眼前
scene: 旅馆房间在六楼，她拉开窗帘，整片湖面就铺在眼前。The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 view 是「景色」（第 1 个义项：从某处能看到的景象）；句意为这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。推开窗后铺开的画面正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 景色；看法；视野
观看；看待

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「观众；观看者」
合成词，义为「观点；视角」
加前缀 re- 构成，义为「回顾；评论」

senses.title: What can be seen from a place
senses.definition: the whole scene that a place allows you to see
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的整体景象
senses.example: The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。
senses.why: To look out is to see; the scene laid before the eyes is the view.
senses.whyCN: 向外看是「看」这个动作，而铺在眼前的那片景象就是 view。

senses.title: A person’s opinion about something
senses.definition: a particular way of thinking about a matter
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的特定想法
senses.example: In my view the plan costs too much.
senses.exampleCN: 在我看来这个计划花费太高。
senses.why: The eye and the mind use one word: what you see from where you stand is what you think from where you stand.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛与头脑共用一个词：从哪个位置看，就从哪个位置想。

senses.title: The range within which something can be seen
senses.definition: the area that can be seen from a point, or the chance to see something
senses.definitionCN: 从一个位置能看见的区域，或看见某物的机会
senses.example: The ship came into view at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时那艘船出现在视野里。
senses.why: A view is not only the picture but the space in which the picture can appear.
senses.whyCN: view 不只是那幅画面，也是画面得以出现的空间。

senses.title: To look at something carefully
senses.definition: to watch or examine something, especially for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有目的地观看或检查某物
senses.example: The committee viewed the site before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前察看了现场。
senses.why: The noun gives a verb: to give a thing your view is to view it.
senses.whyCN: 名词派生动词：把目光给某物，就是去观看它。

senses.title: To regard something in a certain way
senses.definition: to think of something as being a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物视为某一性质的事物
senses.example: Many people view silence as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人把沉默看作同意。
senses.why: When the mind places a thing before itself, the same verb names the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑把一物摆在自身之前端详时，这个动词也用来表示判断。

senses.title: What can be seen in a picture or on a screen
senses.definition: the scene shown in an image, drawing, or display
senses.definitionCN: 图像、图画或屏幕中显示的场景
senses.example: The drawing shows the house from the front view.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画从正面视角画了这座房子。
senses.why: Images repeat the word, naming the angle from which a scene is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 图像沿用了这个词，用来指画面取景的角度。

intro.en: View comes from Old French veue, a seeing, from Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: view 来自古法语 veue（看见），源头是拉丁语 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visus gave the noun of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其过去分词 visus 派生出「所见」的名词。

items.en: French veue named the act of seeing and the sight itself.
items.cn: 法语 veue 既指看的动作，也指所见之物。

items.en: English borrowed it as vewe, later spelled view.
items.cn: 英语借入作 vewe，后来拼作 view。

items.en: The sense widened from sight to the scene before the eyes.
items.cn: 词义从「看」扩展到眼前的景象。

items.en: Opinion and examination joined the family, giving in my view and to view a site.
items.cn: 「看法」与「检查」加入词族，产生 in my view 与 view a site。

note.en: The first group holds words built on view, the second the words for scenes and opinions.
note.cn: 第一组是由 view 构成的词，第二组是表示景象与看法的词。

entries.definition: a person who watches
entries.definitionCN: 观众；观看者

entries.definition: a position from which one thinks
entries.definitionCN: 观点；视角

entries.definition: to look over again
entries.definitionCN: 回顾；评论

entries.definition: more than one opinion
entries.definitionCN: 多种看法

entries.definition: a place as it looks
entries.definitionCN: 景色；场面

entries.definition: the power or act of seeing
entries.definitionCN: 视力；景象

entries.definition: what one thinks
entries.definitionCN: 意见

entries.definition: a broad look over an area
entries.definitionCN: 俯瞰；调查

normalIntro.en: Latin to see becomes both the thing seen and the thought held: the eye and the mind share one short word.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「看」既成为所见之物，也成为所持之见：眼睛与头脑共用一个短词。

normal.en: View is short but the vowel is long: /vjuː/.
normal.cn: view 拼写不长，但元音读长音 /vjuː/。

normal.en: Viewer adds -er for the one watching.
normal.cn: viewer 加 -er 表示观看的人。

normal.en: Viewpoint joins view and point, a place to think from.
normal.cn: viewpoint 由 view 与 point 合成，指思考所站的位置。

normal.en: Review begins with re-, to look again.
normal.cn: review 以 re- 开头，意为再看一遍。

normal.en: In my view is the standard way to give an opinion.
normal.cn: 给出看法时常用 in my view。

abstract.en: See curtains pulled back onto a wide lake.
abstract.cn: 想窗帘被拉开，露出一整片湖。

abstract.en: Picture two people on one hill looking different ways.
abstract.cn: 想一座山上两个人朝不同方向看。

abstract.en: Hear someone say that is how I see it.
abstract.cn: 听有人说，我就是这么看的。

examples.en: From the top of the tower the whole town is in view.
examples.cn: 从塔顶望去，整座小镇尽收眼底。

examples.en: The council viewed the plans with suspicion.
examples.cn: 议会带着怀疑看待这些计划。

examples.en: Her view of the matter changed after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议之后，她对这件事的看法变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「V 呦」——站在山顶比个 V，呦，风景真好看。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ 过去分词 visus → 古法语 veue → 英语 view

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a scene from a window and ends with a judgment in the mind; the verb bridges watching and regarding.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从窗外的景象开始，走到心中的判断；动词则连接了「观看」与「看作」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lake spread out beyond an open window.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的窗外铺开一片湖。

branches.en: The window branch: lake and hills from a room.
branches.cn: 窗户分支：房里望见的湖与山。

branches.en: The opinion branch: my view on the cost.
branches.cn: 看法分支：我对花费的看法。

branches.en: The range branch: a ship heaving into sight.
branches.cn: 范围分支：船驶入视野。

branches.en: The looking branch: viewing a site, and viewing silence as consent.
branches.cn: 观看分支：察看现场，把沉默看作同意。

branches.en: The drawing branch: a house shown from the front view.
branches.cn: 绘图分支：房子的正面视图。

intro.en: The root vid-, vis-, view- means to see; -er, -point, and re- extend the word.
intro.cn: 词根 vid-、vis-、view- 意为看见，-er、-point、re- 扩展这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, passed through French as veue and reaches English as view, with its relatives visible and vision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）经法语 veue 传入英语成为 view，同族还有 visible 与 vision。

items.example: A viewpoint is where one stands to think.
items.exampleCN: viewpoint 是思考所站的位置。

items.example: Preview shows the work before release.
items.exampleCN: preview 在上映前展示作品。
visible 与词根 vis- 同源。

definition_zh: 观点；视角；观察位置
definition_en: a way of thinking about something, or a position from which something is seen
core_image: 两个人在山的两侧，看到不同的坡
scene: 讨论会上，工程师和村民对同一个水坝各说各话，因为他们的立场完全不同。From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
sceneCN: 这里 viewpoint 是「观点、立场」（第 1 个义项：思考某事时所处的角度）；句意为从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。山两侧看到不同坡面的两个人正是这个词的核心。

pos.zh: 观点；视角

derivatives.zh: 合成词的前半部分，义为「看法；景色」
合成词的后半部分，义为「点；位置」
加后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带有特定立场的」（少数用法）

senses.title: A way of thinking about a matter
senses.definition: a particular attitude or set of opinions on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一问题所持的态度或一套看法
senses.example: From a farmer’s viewpoint, the dam is a threat rather than a promise.
senses.exampleCN: 从农民的角度看，这座水坝是威胁而非希望。
senses.why: View gives what one sees and point gives where one stands; together they name the place a judgment comes from.
senses.whyCN: view 给的是所见，point 给的是所站之处；合起来就指判断出自的那个位置。

senses.title: A physical position for observing
senses.definition: the spot from which a scene or object is looked at
senses.definitionCN: 观看某一场景或物体时所处的地点
senses.example: The guide marked the best viewpoint above the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 导游标出了山谷上方最好的观景位置。
senses.why: A painter must choose an eye-level before starting, and that place is literally a viewpoint.
senses.whyCN: 画家动笔前要选定视平线所在的位置，那正是字面意义上的 viewpoint。

senses.title: The angle shown in a picture or film
senses.definition: the camera angle from which a scene is filmed or drawn
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄或绘制场景时所用的机位角度
senses.example: The scene is shot from a child’s viewpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 这场戏是从一个孩子的视角拍的。
senses.why: Film borrows the word to name the eye the camera pretends to be.
senses.whyCN: 电影借用这个词，指镜头假装成为的那只眼睛。

senses.title: In debate, one side of an argument
senses.definition: one of the positions presented in a discussion or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 讨论或争执中所呈现的一个立场
senses.example: Each viewpoint was given ten minutes in the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中每一方立场各给十分钟。
senses.why: When positions are counted and timed, the abstract angle becomes a labelled side.
senses.whyCN: 当各方立场被计数并分配时间时，抽象的角度就成了一条标名的立场。

senses.title: A standpoint supported by evidence
senses.definition: an opinion backed by facts or experience rather than feeling
senses.definitionCN: 以事实或经验为依据而非仅凭感觉的意见
senses.example: Her viewpoint rests on five years of field data.
senses.exampleCN: 她的看法建立在五年实地数据之上。
senses.why: The word suits arguments that can point at something, since point is inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词适合能指向具体证据的论证，因为它本身就含着 point。

intro.en: Viewpoint is an English compound: view, what is seen, plus point, a place.
intro.cn: viewpoint 是英语合成词：view（所见）加 point（位置）。

items.en: Veue, a seeing, reached English as view.
items.cn: 古法语 veue（看见）进入英语成为 view。

items.en: Punctum meant a small hole or a dot, from pungere, to prick.
items.cn: punctum 意为小孔或小点，源自 pungere（刺）。

items.en: French point named a dot or a place on a surface.
items.cn: 法语 point 指平面上的点或位置。

items.en: The compound viewpoint joined the two words for a judging position.
items.cn: 合成词 viewpoint 把两个词合成表示判断的位置。

items.en: It spread from painting and surveying to opinion writing.
items.cn: 它从绘画与测量扩展到议论文章。

note.en: The first group holds the two words that make the compound plus its relatives, the second the near synonyms for opinion.
note.cn: 第一组是构成这个合成词的两个词及相近形式，第二组是「意见」的近义词。

entries.definition: several standpoints
entries.definitionCN: 多种观点

entries.definition: what one sees or thinks
entries.definitionCN: 看法；景色

entries.definition: a dot or place
entries.definitionCN: 点；位置

entries.definition: having a stated stance
entries.definitionCN: 带有立场的

entries.definition: the position from which one judges
entries.definitionCN: 立场

entries.definition: a way of seeing things in proportion
entries.definitionCN: 透视；视角

entries.definition: the direction from which a thing is approached
entries.definitionCN: 角度

entries.definition: a general view of life
entries.definitionCN: 人生观；看法

normalIntro.en: Two plain words welded together: where you view from is what you point at.
normalIntro.cn: 两个普通词焊在一起：从哪里看，就指向什么。

normal.en: Viewpoint is view plus point, and the stress falls on view.
normal.cn: viewpoint 是 view 加 point，重音落在 view。

normal.en: Standpoint is its close twin, made with stand.
normal.cn: standpoint 是它的近义双胞胎，用 stand 构成。

normal.en: It takes from: from my viewpoint.
normal.cn: 前面常接 from：from my viewpoint。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: viewpoints.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：viewpoints。

normal.en: Point at the end hints that reasons can be pointed to.
normal.cn: 结尾的 point 提示理由是可以指出的。

abstract.en: Picture two hikers on opposite slopes, each seeing one side.
abstract.cn: 想两位徒步者站在山坡两侧，各看见一面。

abstract.en: See a camera lowered to a child’s height.
abstract.cn: 想镜头降到孩子的高度。

abstract.en: Hear a speaker say, from where I stand.
abstract.cn: 听人说我站的位置看到的是这样。

examples.en: The article presents the viewpoint of the workers, not the owners.
examples.cn: 这篇文章呈现的是工人的立场，而不是雇主的。

examples.en: Seen from a historical viewpoint, the treaty looks different.
examples.cn: 从历史的视角看，这份条约大不相同。

examples.en: The hilltop is the best viewpoint in the park.
examples.cn: 山顶是公园里最好的观景点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一炮硬」——只有一门炮硬说有理，这就是他的观点。

root: view（看法，源自拉丁 videre「看」）+ point（点，源自拉丁 punctum）→ viewpoint

sensesIntro.en: A seeing plus a place gives a word that covers opinions, camera angles, and the hilltop where you stand to look.
sensesIntro.cn: 「看」加上「位置」，合成一个同时覆盖意见、机位与山顶观景处的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on opposite slopes of one hill.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座山两侧的两个人。

branches.en: The farmer branch: a dam seen as a threat.
branches.cn: 农民分支：水坝被视为威胁。

branches.en: The hilltop branch: the best place to look down.
branches.cn: 山顶分支：俯瞰的最佳位置。

branches.en: The camera branch: a scene at a child’s height.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：孩子高度的场景。

branches.en: The debate branch: ten minutes for each side.
branches.cn: 辩论分支：每方十分钟。

branches.en: The evidence branch: five years of field data.
branches.cn: 证据分支：五年的实地数据。

intro.en: Viewpoint is built from two free words, view and point, each with its own Latin root.
intro.cn: viewpoint 由两个自由词 view 与 point 构成，各自有自己的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Videre, to see, supplies view; punctum, a dot, supplies point; English merely joints them.
latinIntro.cn: videre（看见）提供 view，punctum（点）提供 point，英语只是把二者拼合。

items.example: The second half fixes the place.
A viewpointed essay takes a clear side.
items.exampleCN: 有立场的文章总会偏向一方。

items.example: Standpoint is built the same way.
Perspective comes from per and specere.
items.exampleCN: perspective 来自 per 与 specere。

items.example: Outlook looks outward for a general view.
items.exampleCN: outlook 向外看，指总体看法。

definition_zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的
definition_en: full of physical strength and energy, or strong and forceful
core_image: 晨跑的人大步跨过台阶，呼吸深而稳
scene: 医生看完体检报告，说他恢复得很好，可以恢复剧烈运动了。The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
sceneCN: 这里 vigorous 是「剧烈的、有力的」（第 2 个义项：强度大而有力量）；句意为医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。大步跨台阶、呼吸深稳的晨跑者就是这个词给人的感觉。

pos.zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；强健的

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成名词，义为「精力；活力」（美式 vigor）
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「有力地；精力充沛地」
加前缀 in- 与后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使振奋；使有活力」

senses.title: Full of bodily strength
senses.definition: strong, healthy, and full of energy
senses.definitionCN: 强壮、健康且充满活力
senses.example: At seventy he is still vigorous and walks five miles a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他七十岁仍精力充沛，每天走五英里。
senses.why: Latin vigor meant liveliness and force, and a vigorous person carries both.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vigor 意为活力与力量，精力充沛的人两者兼有。

senses.title: Strong in force or intensity
senses.definition: done with great force or energy
senses.definitionCN: 以很大力量或强度完成的
senses.example: The doctor said he could return to vigorous exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说他可以恢复剧烈运动了。
senses.why: The same force, applied to an activity rather than a person, makes the activity vigorous.
senses.whyCN: 同一股力量若落到活动上而非人身上，活动本身就变得有力、剧烈。

senses.title: Lively and forceful in speech or style
senses.definition: expressed with energy and confidence
senses.definitionCN: 表达得充满能量与自信
senses.example: She made a vigorous defence of the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她为这项计划做了有力的辩护。
senses.why: Language borrows the body and puts its force into argument.
senses.whyCN: 语言借用身体的力量，把它注入论辩之中。

senses.title: Growing strongly
senses.definition: growing fast and healthily, as a plant does
senses.definitionCN: 像植物那样快速而健康地生长
senses.example: Vigorous growth followed the spring rain.
senses.exampleCN: 春雨之后出现了旺盛的生长。
senses.why: What is strong in body is active in growth as well.
senses.whyCN: 强健之物在生长上也同样有劲。

senses.why: A group with vigour turns it into a movement.

intro.en: Vigorous rests on Latin vigor, the liveliness that makes a body act.

items.en: Vigere meant to be lively or to flourish, and vigor was that liveliness.

items.en: French vigour carried the word with the sense of strength.
items.cn: 法语 vigour 带着「力量」的含义承接此词。

items.en: English vigour named bodily force and the force of law alike.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 vigour 既指体力，也指法律的效力。

items.en: The adjective vigorous spread to exercise, argument, and growth.
items.cn: 形容词 vigorous 扩展到运动、论辩与生长。

items.en: American spelling drops the u: vigor, but keeps vigorous.
items.cn: 美式拼写去掉 u 作 vigor，但 vigorous 不变。

note.en: The first group holds the vigour family, the second the words for strength and its lack.

sensesIntro.en: One Latin word for liveliness spreads from a strong body to strong exercise, strong speech, fast growth, and loud public action.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个表示生机的拉丁词，从强健的身体延伸到剧烈的运动、有力的言辞、旺盛的生长与声势浩大的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner taking the steps two at a time.

branches.en: The body branch: a strong man of seventy.
branches.cn: 身体分支：七十岁仍强健的人。

branches.en: The activity branch: back to vigorous exercise.

branches.en: The speech branch: a vigorous defence of the plan.

branches.en: The plant branch: growth after spring rain.

definition_en: to break a law, rule, or agreement, or to treat something sacred with disrespect

scene: 新闻里说，这家公司被查出违反了安全规定。The company was found to have violated safety rules.

senses.title: To break a rule or law
senses.definition: to act against a law, rule, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 做出违背法律、规则或约定的行为
senses.example: The company was found to have violated safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司被查出违反了安全规定。
senses.why: Latin violare meant to treat with force, and treating a rule with force is breaking it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 violare 意为以强力对待，用强力对待规则就是违反规则。

senses.title: To break into what belongs to another
senses.definition: to intrude on rights, privacy, or a person
senses.definitionCN: 侵入他人的权利、隐私或人身
senses.example: The reporter had violated her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 那位记者侵犯了她的隐私。
senses.why: When force crosses a boundary that belongs to someone else, the word shifts from rules to persons.
senses.whyCN: 当强力越过属于他人的边界时，这个词就从规则转向了人。

senses.title: To treat something sacred with disrespect
senses.definition: to show contempt for a holy place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对神圣的场所或事物表示轻慢
senses.example: Touching the altar was thought to violate the temple.
senses.exampleCN: 人们认为触碰祭坛是亵渎神庙。
senses.why: The oldest use is about holy places, where force feels most shocking.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法针对圣地，那里施加强力最令人震惊。

senses.title: To break a promise or agreement
senses.definition: to fail to keep what one has agreed to

senses.whyCN: 契约是双方一起写下的规则，破坏它用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To disturb the peace of a place

senses.definitionCN: 打破某处的安静或秩序
senses.example: A siren violated the silence of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 一声警笛打破了夜的寂静。
senses.why: Quiet and order are also boundaries, and force across them is a violation.
senses.whyCN: 宁静与秩序也是边界，强力越过它们同样是侵犯。
